I confirm that EP4382  has been over utilized and causing the packet loss for the customer. Please be aware that due to the current cable faults we do loose capacity in that region. We are see if we can fine-tune the route. More updates to follow. Any questions or concerns, please feel free to contact  me using the details in my signature.

 

https://jira.pccwglobal.com/browse/AS3491-4257

 

 

*[APCN2**]*

*+APCN2 Segment 7 cable fault+*

*APCN2 S7 (Shantou, China – Tanshui, Taiwan) has been down at 21:26GMT, 3-Jan. 2021. The fault location is estimated at 179Km from Shantou cable landing station. PCCW Global has 5 customer services that are being affected. According to Cable NOC, Cable Ship Asean Restorer is assigned for the repair operations after completion of SJC S13 Op#10 repair and the tentative repair window is expected 12 – 15 Feb and more updates to follow.*

 

 ** 

*[SJC**]*

*+SJC Segment 13 suspected cable fault+*

*SJC S13 (Chikura, Japan – BU 6) has been down at 20:04GMT, 12-Nov. 2020. The fault location is estimated at 980Km from Shantou cable landing station or between 3161Km and 3089Km from Chikura cable landing station. All traffic terminating / transiting in Japan is currently down and PCCW Global has 25 customer services that are being affected. According to Cable NOC, because of the sudden ocean swell which caused the cable to be parted, grapnel drive is required to recover cable towards Chikura end for testing before making the 4^th^ joint. Therefore, the tentative completion date is slipped to 4-Feb.*

Manual filters on the RRs (doesn't matter if regional or cross-regional) have to go away. Route propagation has to be handled on the edge, rather than from those central points.
That's the plan since the very beginning and the primary reason why we've developed the new route-policies (all of them).

We knew it would have been a rather long transition. Other than the iBGP sessions with the RRs, we also had to reconfigure all of the eBGP with peers and customers. So, in order to avoid outages, we've decided to keep the manual filtering on the RRs up until the transition was over.  

But, now that CE and IPC have completed their quests and all of the sessions are using the new policies, manual filters are causing more harm than good and have to be removed.

Hi Morgan,

 

I hope you are doing good!

 

My findings are below:

 

Seems as the main issue on your line card 3 was linked with a heartbeat.

 

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Jan  7 00:18:17.145 : shelfmgr[409]: %PLATFORM-SHELFMGR_HAL-6-HEARTBEAT_ALERT : 0/3/CPU0 heartbeat, non-responsive for 112 seconds. (Threshold: 220 seconds), Send/Rcv Seq#: 21898/21842

 

Regarding EOBC error, this was a transit communication problem between RSPs that already cleared by itself:

 


 RP/0/RSP1/CPU0:Jan  7 00:17:41.359 : pfm_node_rp[364]: %PLATFORM-DIAGS-3-SRSP_ACTIVE_EOBC_FAILED : Set|online_diag_rsp[213109]|SRSP active EOBC Test(0x2000002)|failure threshold is 10, rack slot(s) failed: (0/3) RP/0/RSP1/CPU0:Jan  7 00:17:44.359 : pfm_node_rp[364]: %PLATFORM-DIAGS-3-SRSP_STANDBY_EOBC_FAILED : Set|online_diag_rsp[213109]|SRSP standby EOBC Test(0x2000001)|failure threshold is 10, rack slot(s) failed: (0/3) 

 

RP/0/RSP1/CPU0:Jan  7 00:18:58.394 : pfm_node_rp[364]: %PLATFORM-DIAGS-3-SRSP_ACTIVE_EOBC_FAILED : Clear|online_diag_rsp[213109]|SRSP active EOBC Test(0x2000002)|failure threshold is 10, rack slot(s) failed: (0/3)RP/0/RSP1/CPU0:Jan  7 00:19:01.394 : pfm_node_rp[364]: %PLATFORM-DIAGS-3-SRSP_STANDBY_EOBC_FAILED : Clear|online_diag_rsp[213109]|SRSP standby EOBC Test(0x2000001)|failure threshold is 10, rack slot(s) failed: (0/3)

 

 

Just to describe the overall operation of the Heart Beat, it is an internal signaling protocol that runs at the Ether Out of Band Channel (EOBC) to maintain constant communication between the control planes of the cards, in this case from the RP0 (active) to the RP1 (standby).

 

If router doesn’t  have response from heart beat it will reload itself in order to recover LC3.

 

At the moment the LC is working fine, so in this case this could just be a transitory issue. Outputs below:

Hi Max,

 

We are suspecting an issue with ext_ram_freq & shmoo files. (This is just a suspection we are doing more internal discussion to come up with POA).

 

Below is the brief information about ext_ram_freq and Shmoo file:

 

ext_ram_freq is one of the dram parameters... that effects the packets that pass through dram... shmoo is like during init, it tunes the dram parameters during initialization. to save time during boot, it saves those parameters in a file called shmoo file... so that next time devices boots it reuses those parameters saved in the file. with ext_ram_freq 1600 you get one type of parameters, with 1066 you get different type of parameters.. if the device in the factory got tuned with some different image it would have tuned with 1600 and saved in the shmoo file. now when it is booting at the customer it would reuse those parameters instead of values that were tuned at 1066 parameters making the configured freq as 1600 when it should be 1066.

 

now in this case, we are not sure that shmoo file you are using was generated from 711 as it was shipped with the image and shmoo that were generated at factory.

 

This is the reason I have asked you for day1 OS version.

 

Thanks & Regards,

Jan 28, 2021 19:23;712020:1c4de9a1-879b-434d-ac02-16ce22b36c58;{quote}Navin Sinha (navisinh) <[navisinh@cisco.com|mailto:navisinh@cisco.com]> 於 2021年1月28日 17:21 寫道：
Hi Max,
 
Hope you are doing Great..!!
Please find the RFO below:
 
*Problem Description:*
Unexpected Reboot on NCS540
 
*Trigger Point:*
 
The FIA ASIC has hit a multibit error in the external DRAM packet memory of the ASIC. The system went for a hard reset to recover from this fault. This is the expected action for this error.
ext_ram_freq should be 1066 and shmoo file should be generated based on that value.
 
ext_ram_freq is one of the dram parameters... that effects the packets that pass through dram... shmoo is like during init, it tunes the dram parameters during initialization. to save time during boot, it saves those parameters in a file called shmoo file... so that next time devices boots it reuses those parameters saved in the file. with ext_ram_freq 1600 you get one type of parameters, with 1066 you get different type of parameters.. if the device in the factory got tuned with some different image it would have tuned with 1600 and saved in the shmoo file. now when it is booting at the customer it would reuse those parameters instead of values that were tuned at 1066 parameters making the configured freq as 1600 when it should be 1066.
 
We checked the shmoo files and found the router got a fault shmoo files with the wrong value from the factory itself.
 
*Workaround:*
The solution to recover is to retune the parameters present in the shmoo files.
 
To retune the parameters below is the procedure:
 
attach loc 0/0/CPU0
cd /mnt/shmoo/ 
ls fia_*_shmoo_0 
rm -rf fia_ddr_shmoo_0
exit 
admin hw-module location all reloads
 
after retuning the parameters the issue was not seen.

Jacky, Sandeep,

*Cc:* "Kostas Yiotis" <[kyiotis@pccwglobal.com|mailto:kyiotis@pccwglobal.com]>, "Bia, Benjamin" <[bbia@pccwglobal.com|mailto:bbia@pccwglobal.com]>, "Caci, Pierfrancesco" <[pcaci@pccwglobal.com|mailto:pcaci@pccwglobal.com]>, "Grassot, Wilfrid" <[wgrassot@pccwglobal.com|mailto:wgrassot@pccwglobal.com]>, "Jordan, James" <[JJordan@pccwglobal.com|mailto:JJordan@pccwglobal.com]>, "PCCW Global" <[mobilityengineering@pccwglobal.com|mailto:mobilityengineering@pccwglobal.com]>
*Sent:* Monday, October 26, 2020 4:15:28 PM
*Subject:* Re: WRT : Globalview issues with changing ifIndex values / incorrect sampling rate

 

Hello,

 

First of all, thank you for your email! It's extremely detailed.

 

I have to admit i didn't know nothing about Interface Table, so i made some researches and i have bad news: That feature is Cisco's only.

 

Here's what i found: Interface table makes use of Netflow field values 82 (IF_NAME) and 83 (IF_DESC). And, although they got eventually adopted by IANA (URL: [https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipfix/ipfix.xhtml]), they're not supported by any of the major vendors out there if not by Cisco.

Here's the two that i took for reference:
 * [https://www.juniper.net/documentation/en_US/junos/topics/reference/general/flowmonitoring-output-formats-version9-solutions.html]
 * [https://documentation.nokia.com/html/0_add-h-f/93-0073-HTML/7750_SR_OS_Router_Configuration_Guide/Cflowd_cli.pdf]

 

They have the most advanced network operating systems along with Cisco. If they don't support it, then i doubt others do.

 

It also looks like the IETF took a different approach back in 2017 with RFC8038 ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8038]) that I quote: "specifies a way to complement IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) Data Records with Management Information Base (MIB) objects, avoiding the need to define new IPFIX Information Elements for existing MIB objects that are already fully specified".

It's sounds exactly what we need, but i can't find any vendor supporting it. So it's a dead end.

 

It is also worth to note that the feature has been introduced by Cisco with IOS-XR 5.2.0 and some of our BRs still run 4.3.4. And I know that your plan is to use VARs only and that you can migrate all of the circuits off the BRs just to make the above interface table, but we've been asked to not to get stuck with a single vendor.

 

I am sorry, we can't turn it on. 

 

While, regarding the sampling rate, those are very old devices.

I've tried to change to value on one and IOS has rejected the command because the exporter is in use.

br01.hkg02(config-sampler)#mode random 1 out-of 4000% sampler: Failed to set sampler mode: Object is in usebr01.hkg02(config-sampler)#

 

Looks like we need a CMR.

I am writing an email to Sandeep and Jacky with you on copy.

 

Regards

*Sent:* Monday, October 26, 2020 2:45:05 PM
*Subject:* WRT : Globalview issues with changing ifIndex values / incorrect sampling rate

 

Hello all,

 

As per our latest discussion, I have the following findings to report.

 

I’ve found the following routers that have a sampling rate of 1/4096 instead of 1/4000 :

 

br01.hkg02

br01.hkg14

br03.bkk01

var01.jnb01

var05.mpm02

 

If you want me to open a ticket about that, please let me know how to do that ( which project / any features I should link to on your side / etc ) and I’ll do it.

 

Regarding sending the interface table and the sampler table via netflow, I did run a small PoC for it. Unfortunately our virtualized IOS-XR router ( xrv9000 ) does not support netflow. I did manage to successfully set it up on a virtualized IOS-XE router ( csr1000v ) though. I’ve attached screenshots that show a packet capture of the data as they’re received by the netflow collector. I can also provide a sample pcap if needed. The vendor documentation for it is as follows :

IOS-XE : [https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/fnetflow/configuration/15-mt/fnf-15-mt-book/cfg-de-fnflow-exprts.html]
IOS-XR : [https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/routers/asr9000/software/asr9k-r6-3/netflow/configuration/guide/b-netflow-cg-asr9000-63x/b-netflow-cg-asr9000-63x_chapter_010.html#concept_C4F69023A1BA468D89F4025FD9E85B5E]

 

The IOS-XE one is somewhat more generic, only mentioning options templates in examples. The IOS-XR one is a little bit more comprehensive. The configuration I used for IOS-XE ( only depicting what is different from our current configuration ) was :

 

flow exporter NETFLOW_EXPORT

option interface-table

option sampler-table

 

According to the documentation, the same configuration for IOS-XE would be :

 

flow exporter-map NETFLOW_EXPORT

version v9

  options interface-table

  options sampler-table

 

As per the discussion, it would probably be preferable to get that information from another source that already has it, but we’ve at least proven it’s feasible. Whether it could actually work at our scale or have any other implications, I defer to you.

 

If you want me to check anything else, please let me know.

 

Kind regards,

Dear, Max

 

As the information you provide, I have an update for this case.

 

*Problem Description:*
 # Log alarm:

.Oct 15 01:49:27.398: %IOSXE-2-PLATFORM: F0: cpp_cp: QFP:0.0 Thread:044 TS:00000155980516238239 %HAL_PKTMEM-2-OUT_OF_RESOURCES:

2.This device auto reload.

 

*Problem Analysis:*
 # We can find the Gi0/0/3 the fc: 0x01 through the show command.

Fc value 0x01 indicates that there is a XOFF flow-control message from SIP to BQS for this particular interface.

XOFF means stop sending traffic. Hence, BQS will not dequeue the packets until an XON flow-control message is sent by the SIP.

 

I discovered it was actually interface gig 0/0/3 the interface that was being oversubscribed:

var03.los01#$qs schedule output default interface gi0/0/3 hierarchy detail  

Interface: *GigabitEthernet0/0/3* QFP: 0.0 if_h: 153 Num Queues/Schedules: 2

----------skip---------

        defer: 0x00, fc: 0x01, sfc: 0x00            ---------------->>>>>fc: 0x01,  (REM Congestion Info)

      REM Timestamp Info:

        exp: 0x02, slip_value: 0x343c, virtual_time: 0x0f92

        seid: 0x106

 
 # There is no specific problem to be addressed, this bug is for Documentation. 
Details are provided below but the summary is that the router ran out of packet buffers because the interface is oversubscribed with pak_priority traffic. 
This could be caused by incorrect configuration leading to control packets oversubscribing the interface or in very rare cases malicious traffic intended for denial-of-service.
Since the ASR1K does not drop PAK_PRIORITY packets, they can easily oversubscribe the packet buffers when there is a storm. It is recommended to configure the control plane policer to prevent from malicious traffic.

 

[https://bst.cloudapps.cisco.com/bugsearch/bug/CSCug42528/?referring_site=ss&dtid=osscdc000283]

 

*Action Plan:*

a/ It is suggested as best practice to apply control plane policy to prevent from malicious traffic affecting control packets.

You can find the Control Plane Policing Implementation Best Practices and ASR1000 Control Plane Policing Guide in following links:

  [http://www.cisco.com/web/about/security/intelligence/coppwp_gs.html]

 

b/ Since the device will automatically restart, we can configure EEM or EPC to automatically collect information when this problem occurs again.

Next time a log indicating “%HAL_PKTMEM-2-OUT_OF_RESOURCES” is seen, EEM will automatically collect information.

 

You can reference the following link about the *EPC: (EPC just capture the gi0/0/3)*

[https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/ios-nx-os-software/ios-embedded-packet-capture/116045-productconfig-epc-00.html]

Hi Max,

 

Per our discussion over the phone, we found there is a physical connection between var03.los01 and cr01.ldn12. However, they could not reach out to each other and the ISIS neighbor is also down so far. Moreover, the counter of pause input on GigabitEthernet0/0/3 has been increasing although there is no traffic carried on GigabitEthernet0/0/3. We hence suspect that it might be the cause after studying some similar internal cases. To make ASR1K stable, we suggest shutting down the port of GigabitEthernet0/0/3 or unplug this link on var03.los01 before this submarine cable recovers and works normally and stability.

I understand that you have made GigabitEthernet0/0/3 disconnected, would appreciate it if you could help monitor the counter of pause input of GigabitEthernet0/0/3 and packet buffers memory utilization via the command "sh platform hardware qfp active bqs 0 packet-buffer utilization".

Meanwhile, I will work with Cisco team to find out the root-cause and workarounds to avoid the issue that reoccurs.

Feel free to ping me. Thanks.

 

Regards,

Michael

As we have discussed in Webex meeting, even if the policy-map AWS-Test is configured on output direction, the egress policy-map stats isactually collected at ingress VOQ admission itself.

Any drops across the pipeline(Fabric, ETPP, EGQ) till egress won’t get accounted. So the packets are still likely to get dropped inside clbr01.tok02, after the ingress NPU processing.

c/ when the BQS buffer is full, the device can’t work normally

Hi Max,

 

*_Problem info:_*

a/ The device will display huge amount of frame in “pause input” during issue interface which will lead all packet-buffer full as following:

0 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles

 

0 input errors, 0 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored

 

0 watchdog, 661124 multicast, 309089901 pause input                                                                               

 

b/ During the issue time have following resource error log :

%IOSXE-2-PLATFORM: F0: cpp_cp: QFP:0.0 Thread:044 TS:00000155980516238239 %HAL_PKTMEM-2-OUT_OF_RESOURCES:

monitor and collect the information

 

*_Problem analysis:_*

From the information and error counter we had discuss with DE.

As we discuss with DE this issue hit BUG CSCuw94653.

 

Following are the link of BUG:

[https://bst.cloudapps.cisco.com/bugsearch/bug/CSCuw94653]

 

*_Action plan:_*

 

*_a/ Use following workaround:_*

>> Shutting down the affected interface will protect it against buildup, If the packets aren't cleared out by ?shut? command, disconnect the cable and they will drain out.

>> A router reload will serve the same purpose (drain out packets) and fix the problem until next build up.

>> Verify why neighboring device is sending excessive pause frames, The IOS CLI doesn't have an explicit disable command but if the other end does, then the router will disable it on the next auto-negotiation sequence.

 

*_b/ Upgrade version to fixed list._*

  *_Be attention that after upgrade could avoid BUG but still impact this interface(If peer still send pause packets)._*

Please feel free to contact me again if you have any other question.

Typically CE will configure the BR-SW and VAR-SW trunks once the 1st customer is provisioned.

Remember NCS5K as a L2 fan-out switch uses l2vpn concepts for local bridging and switching.

I've configured the trunk between br01.mil02-sw04.mil02 as follows. Please complete the descriptions and modify accordingly.

On sw04.mil02:

interface Bundle-Ether3.100 l2transport
 description pending activation ntt peer-490

 encapsulation dot1q 100

 rewrite ingress tag pop 1 symmetric

!

interface Bundle-Ether4
 description pending activation ntt peer-490

 l2transport

 !

l2vpn
 bridge group NTT

 bridge-domain NTT

 interface Bundle-Ether4

 !

 interface Bundle-Ether3.100

 !

On br01.mil02:

interface Bundle-Ether3.100
 description pending activation ntt peer-490

 service-policy input IPserv

 ipv6 unreachables disable

 lldp

 transmit disable

 !

Sep 29, 2020 08:34;637dc55c77acd224b33e37b7;Hi Roger,

No other filesystem as an option except harddisk can be chosen, so the filesystem is harddisk.
 
var01.nyc06#request ?
  platform  Request platform actions
 
var01.nyc06#request platform ?
  hardware  Request platform hardware actions
  software  Request platform software actions
 
var01.nyc06#request platform hardware ?
  filesystem  Request filesystem actions
 
var01.nyc06#request platform hardware filesystem ?
  harddisk:       Disk name
  stby-harddisk:  Disk name
 
var01.nyc06#request platform hardware filesystem harddisk: ?
  destroy  Request to erase/destroy entire filesystem
  error    Tune error parameters
  offline  Request to take disk offline
  online   Request to bring disk online
 
var01.nyc06#
 
Here is the example for this command:
Router#request platform hardware filesystem harddisk: online 
 
%This operation may take some time, please be patient
 
%Error: harddisk: already online
Router#

Regards,
Michael

Hi Max,

 

Hope this mail find you well!

Thanks for your patience and please refer to following:

 

1.Standby card become NSR not ready before the LDP/PW down.

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Aug  4 01:12:03.745 : rmf_svr[385]: %HA-REDCON-1-STANDBY_NOT_READY : standby card is NOT ready

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Aug  4 01:12:03.970 : rmf_svr[385]: %HA-REDCON-6-STANDBY_CONNECTION_DOWN : connection to standby card is DOWN

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Aug  4 01:12:54.848 : rmf_svr[385]: %HA-REDCON-1-STANDBY_NOT_READY : standby card is NOT ready

 

 

2.Take LDP Peer 63.218.206.9 as instance.

LDP lost its adjacency to the peer , and PW went down.

 

Aug  4 01:13:38.258 l2vpn/atom 0/RSP1/CPU0 t1  ATOM:3494: P [63.218.206.9]: LDP receive close (LDP GS 0)

Aug  4 01:13:38.258 l2vpn/atom 0/RSP1/CPU0 t1  ATOM:220: Peer [63.218.206.9] clr LDP flags: clear_lsp_up 0

Aug  4 01:13:38.258 l2vpn/atom 0/RSP1/CPU0 t1  ATOM:3222: PW [63.218.206.9,118780]: Marked stale for GR remote-lbl=33898

Aug  4 01:14:35.656 l2vpn/atom 0/RSP1/CPU0 t1  ATOM:286: PW [63.218.206.9,118780]: PW state changed to down

 

 

For the NSR behavior in ASR9K is like this:

 

-In the receive direction both RSPs are interested in LDP packets.

-In the transmit direction the active sends the packets to the standby RSP via NSR

-At this point the active and standby constantly update each other regarding TCP/LDP states

-It is the Standby RSP that ultimately sends the TCP packet out to the peer.

 

 

However the standby RSP became stable until 01:33 that matches the recovery time of the PW.

 

Standby node last went not ready Tue Aug  4 01:12:03 2020: 2 weeks, 6 days, 2 hours, 29 minutes ago

Standby node last went ready Tue Aug  4 01:33:26 2020: 2 weeks, 6 days, 2 hours, 8 minutes ago

Also when I did research in our database fund many DDTs that are related to L2VPN on such lower release we are running on.

I would suggest to upgrade to the new release asap since 434 in already EOM on 2016 and EOS on April 30 2020.

Hi Max,

 

We checked some internal resource, unfortunately, we could not find any known bug related to this issue on XE 3.6.3E, which is caused this po11 flapping. However, we found the most cases were caused by L1 connection.

According to the logs of sw11.hkg04,  the port-channel11 on sw11.hkg04 was flapping during the outage. However, we didn’t have the logs about the member port  Te6/4 and  Te3/1 since the member ports haven’t been configured with command “logging event link-status”.

And after checking the logs on var01.hkg15, there are no existing logs-related to port-channel flapping on var01.hkg15 at this moment. We hence cannot analyse the possible cause on var01.hkg15 as well. Could you please fetch these logs from your remote Syslog servers?

From the configuration perspective, as mentioned above, we suggest configuring logging event link-status on both ports of sw11.hkg04 as below, which will generate the syslog message when the link flaps and the corresponding logs can be used to do the troubleshooting.

 

_sw11.hkg04:_

_interface TenGigabitEthernet3/1_

_logging event link-status_

_!_

_interface TenGigabitEthernet6/4_

_logging event link-status_

_!_

 

In addition, please raise a TAC case to investigate further.

Feel free to ping us. Thanks.

 

Regards,

Michael

Hi Max,

 

Yes, if you want to enable system logging of interface state-change events on all interfaces in the system, please execute the logging event link-status global command in global configuration mode.

 

We have reviewed the logs, according to the logs highlighted in red on var01.hkg15, it appears that port-channel11 was down because bundled ports (0) doesn't meet min-links. However there is no link up/down related logs on interconnect interfaces(te0/0/0 and te1/1/0), and also there is no log such as _TenGigabitEthernet1/1/0 taken out of port-channel11_.

If the traffic is overload and caused output drops under these port, it can cause the lacp packets being dropped and produce the error logs.

 

Microbursts are patterns or spikes of traffic that take place in a relatively short time interval(generally sub-second) causing network interfaces to temporarily become oversubscribed and drop traffic. While bursty traffic is fairly common in networks and in most cases is handled by buffers, in some cases, the spike in traffic is more than the buffer and interface can handle.

#show int Te 3/1 | i is up | drops

#show int Te 6/4 | i is up | drops

If it is the normal traffic, we can add more ports to the port-channel to increase the bandwidth.

If the traffic is not required from a specific source, then we can filter those traffic by ACL of removing the source.

Jun 15, 2020 17:06;712020:1c4de9a1-879b-434d-ac02-16ce22b36c58;{quote}Malpas, Jean <jmalpas@pccwglobal.com> 於 2020年6月15日 15:51 寫道：
Hi Max,
 
Routing convergence could be the root cause indeed.
 
FYI, we faced the same issue with cr01.jnb01 and cr02.jnb01(ASR9006’s) few months ago.
 
There has been a lot of IP Backbone outages due to fiber cut.
 
The routing table changed a lot due to the IP BBone’s flapped, this can cause IS-IS failure/stuck/held.
 
I tried to restart the IS-IS protocol but nothing happened, so the last option was a reload of cr01.jnb01 and cr02.jnb01.
 
Note the TX supplier played with loops to troubleshoot, see the log files in attachment showing flaps of Uplinks of LOS01 to EU or down to CPT01.
Best regards.

 *Subject:* RE: MPLS Duplicate addresses in var06.sin02 AS3491-3026

 

Hello TAC

 

 

Please see below

 

For the “%ROUTING-LDP-4-PEER_DUP_ADDRS : VRF 'default' (0x60000000)” message on var06.sin02, it just tells you that neighbor 202.123.37.182 (a targeted ldp session is formed with that neighbor) is advertising label binding for prefix 10.10.10.1, while some other ldp neighbor has already advertised label binding for the same prefix. If you check the current ldp neighbors, you can find that 198.18.8.18 (a targeted ldp session is formed with that neighbor) has already advertised to var06.sin02 the label binding for 10.10.10.1. That explains why you saw the above message.

 

Anyhow, the message does not necessarily indicate anything abnormal or harmful. It is just to remind you to check whether you have made a configuration mistake or not. In your case, as 10.10.10.1 is NOT learned from any routing protocol and is not installed as a route on var06.sin02, the label binding for 10.10.10.1 is of no use on var06.sin02 and thus you can safely ignore the above message even if duplicate address is advertised by more than one ldp peer.

 

(2)

For the “%IP-4-DUPADDR: Duplicate address 10.5.4.166 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0.110, sourced by 1880.902b.d03f” message on var02.hkg14, it indicates that someone else (with mac address 1880.902b.d03f) on that network is using the ip address of 10.5.4.166 (which is the address configured on var02.hkg14 Gig0/0/0.110). After checking, mac address 1880.902b.d03f actually refers to BDI110 on sw03.hkg14. So, I guess interface BDI110 on sw03.hkg14 somehow got accidentally “no shut”, and that might have triggered the above message. In fact, I don’t see the point why sw03.hkg14 BDI110 is configured with 10.5.4.166 instead of 10.5.4.165 even though it is in admin-shut state now. You may consider tweaking the ip address on sw04.hkg14 to prevent the issue.

Hi Max,

 

As mentioned by Michael, without RT filtering for VPNv4 (i.e., when “no bgp default route-target filter” is configured), an ASR1K with only 4GB memory serving as VPNv4 PE may easily get memory exhausted provided that the current number of VPNv4 routes in PCCWG has reached about 1 million.

 

So, with the current number of vpnv4 routes in your network, we’d suggest you unconfigure “no bgp default route-target filter” on any ASR1K with only 4GB memory. If you must have “no bgp default route-target filter” on an ASR1K running vpnv4 (e.g., when it has to serve as an Inter-AS Option-B ASBR), please ensure that ASR1K has sufficient memory (e.g. 16GB memory) to hold all the concerned vpnv4 routes.

 

Thanks.

Eric

column1: External prefix preferred over internal routes
column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
A prefix learned by GTT was preferred over the internal route generated within PCCWG.

Prefix 63.218.156.0/23 is redistributed into BGP  by cr04.syd02 and advertised to the internet via the local transit with VOCUS in Australia.

That session is configured so that the prefixes we announce are originated by AS198148  rather than AS3491. 

As a result when VOCUS advertises  63.218.156.0/23 to their transits and their transits re-advertise it to us, we receive it back as if it is originated from an outside network.

 

Because of the way the administrative distance is configured on Cisco routers, eBGP routes are preferred over iBGP and ISIS routes and thus our network starts believing the route is external. Thus generating blackholes.

The below proves what i've described:
{noformat}
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:br02.syd02#sh route 63.218.156.0
Thu Apr 30 13:20:18.338 GMT
Routing entry for 63.218.156.0/23
  Known via "bgp 65004", distance 20, metric 100
  Tag 3257, type external
  Installed Apr 30 13:19:56.649 for 00:00:21
  Routing Descriptor Blocks
    103.232.18.177, from 103.232.18.177, BGP external
      Route metric is 100
  No advertising protos.

a/ rmf_svr[385]: %HA-REDCON-1-STANDBY_NOT_READY : standby card is NOT ready

These messages may appear for many different reasons, and does not typically imply any kind of problem. The most common time this is seen is when doing configuration changes.

 

b/ statsd_manager_g[1128]: %MGBL-IFSTATS-4-COLLECTOR_TIMEOUT : A stats collector has timed out during a request:

*Subject:* Re: 688908177 : BGP process crashed on var02.hkg08

 

Hi Max,

 

Thank you for your information. Here is the update for you.

 

*Problem Description:*

BGP process got crashed with core dump.

 

*Problem Analysis:*

1.After decode the core dump and analye all the information, I found a known DDTS to introduce this issue.

 

bgp mem leak in "Path Received Label" with sh bgp vrf neighbor advertised-routes

CSCvp70693

Description

Symptom:

BGP process can leak memory block as shown by this command :

 

sh memory heap dllname  | I Label

...

Block Allocated List:

Total      Total      Block      Name/ID/Caller

Usize      Size       Count

...

0x00012180 0x00048600 0x00004860  Path Received Label

 

when user types the following command :

 

sh bgp vrf  neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes

 

Conditions:

Seen when typing the command :

 

sh bgp vrf  neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes

or

sh bgp vrf  advertised neighbor a.b.c.d

 

and the advertised-routes have a receive label from vpnv4 address-family

 

Workaround:

refrain/reduce usage of this command

 

Further Problem Description:

If repeated continually on Provider Edge router with lot of prefixes, this can ultimately consumes all memory , up to the rlimit threshold, which will cause a bgp process crash.

[https://bst.cloudapps.cisco.com/bugsearch/bug/CSCvp70693]

*Subject:* Re: VAR02.HKG08 - BGP instability - INC000001734912

 

Hi Ryan and TAC,

 

Per Cisco TAC investigation, var02.hkg08 hit a BGP memory leak bug when use "sh bgp vrf  neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes” reparably(trigger details please see following). 

 

We did encountered same bug in var06.sin02 last year, we did stop the script and waiting the bug fix SMU. cisco just released the SMU a couple of weeks ago. as you know arrange maintenances to upgrade the routers within AS3491 need spend many time.

 

I observed someone collecting all VRF BGP neighbors advertised routes every half hour, can you stop the collecting script or run script once per day temporarily for the workaround?

 

 

 

Cisco Bug report———————————————

 

*Problem Description:*

BGP process got crashed with core dump.

 

*Problem Analysis:*

1.After decode the core dump and analye all the information, I found a known DDTS to introduce this issue.

 

bgp mem leak in "Path Received Label" with sh bgp vrf neighbor advertised-routes

CSCvp70693

Description

Symptom:

BGP process can leak memory block as shown by this command :

 

sh memory heap dllname  | I Label

...

Block Allocated List:

Total      Total      Block      Name/ID/Caller

Usize      Size       Count

...

0x00012180 0x00048600 0x00004860  Path Received Label

 

when user types the following command :

 

sh bgp vrf  neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes

 

Conditions:

Seen when typing the command :

 

sh bgp vrf  neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes

or

sh bgp vrf  advertised neighbor a.b.c.d

 

and the advertised-routes have a receive label from vpnv4 address-family

 

Workaround:

refrain/reduce usage of this command

 

Further Problem Description:

If repeated continually on Provider Edge router with lot of prefixes, this can ultimately consumes all memory , up to the rlimit threshold, which will cause a bgp process crash.

[https://bst.cloudapps.cisco.com/bugsearch/bug/CSCvp70693]

 

2.From the cli history,show bgp vrf cli was executed with high frequency.

 

3.As discussed with Eric,PCCWG hit the same issue last year and Cisco NOS team raised a SMU request accordingly. The SMU is now available to fix the issue. Cisco NOS team will share the details very soon

 

*Action Plan:*

1.NOS team will share the details about this fix soon.

2.Currently,please follow the workaround to refrain/reduce usage of “show bgp vrf neighbors a.b.c.d advertised-routes”

Jul 10, 2020 23:14;712020:1f665f07-4e1f-4d0a-930a-a8eeeba91d75;Hi all
 Let me clarify here further, we have implemented the changes in workflow as part of https://jira.pccwglobal.com/browse/CTP-427.

Workflow changes are as below:

We added new steps to track whether provisioning of reserved port is completed or not by pre-sales. All the pending provisioning tickets should be tracked by Pre-sales department/ requestor who is serving the customer and change the status accordingly. If pre-sales will not update the ticket due to reason customer really didn't come back after reserving the port and/or pre-sales didn't provisioned the port then port reservation ticket will be automatically expired and ticket will move to close status. 
 when ticket is in pending provisioning there is SLA clock ticking for 4 months and if status is not updated then it will expire and move ticket to expired stage. At Expired stage if port is not provisioned then reserved port should be made free and ticket should be closed regardless. 

Note: We have one known issue with undo- transition which doesn't reset the clock,So if you clicked In provisioning by mistake and try to move back ticket using un-do transition SLA clock is not get reset. I have reported it to the vendor, vendor is still working on further developing the code.

Let me know if you need further clarification.

My understanding is the preliminary cause of the earlier incident with regards to Hinet not have Link-loss detection enabled and us having to remove the static routes on some of their links to prevent route blackholing has been resolved?

I also understand we are augmenting peering capacity by adding 10GE ports at HKG15.

Will that resolve this problem ticket and should the incident and problem tickets just be closed and this handled via the peering project?

Regards,
Sandeep
column2089:
Apr 09, 2020 22:31;59f78fce068cd6328f465a66;[~accountid:635a238a928dc277b90528da],

There were 2 issues behind the blackholing. First is the link does not propagate fault, the second is we're using eBGP multihop to load balance the traffic between the 2 links on br04.hkg05.

We've already started a project to convert the multihop sessions to LACP and we're keeping track of the progress at this URL: https://jira.pccwglobal.com/browse/PEER-443

The port i've requested on BR03.HKG15 is not for a new peering link, rather is for relocating the existing on BR02.HKG15 so that we can create a 3x10GE LAG.

All of the upgrades mentioned in https://jira.pccwglobal.com/browse/PEER-416 are on hold until Q3-Q4 2020 because of HiNET.

Please keep in mind that with HiNET everything takes forever and a trip to their office (I personally go there along with [~accountid:70121:aaf8df1e-6215-4d06-9e63-fa01e91c6e44] every January).

We can keep this ticket open if you like to, but i would not expect any upgrade up until end of this year.

column2097:
Apr 09, 2020 22:12;59f78fce068cd6328f465a66;The 31st of March 2 of the peering links between PCCWG and HiNET went down because of cable cut. That in turn has triggered blackholing on br04.hkg05

Links are:
 # 
h3. br03.hkg15: TenGigE0/6/0/17

 # 
h3. br04.hkg05: TenGigE0/3/0/9

That on br03.hkg15 was restored, while that on br04.hkg05 is still down.

After receiving complaints from our customers one of our engineers has manually removed br04.hkg05: TenGigE0/3/0/9 from the active links thus resolving the issue.

To get into the details, there's 2 reasons because the blackhole was triggered on br04.hkg05. First the underlying TX link (provied half and half by PCCWG and HiNET) does not propagate faults. The other is we makes use of eBGP multihop to load balance the traffic between the 2 links on BR05.HKG05.

We've started a project to switch from eBGP multihop to LACP a few months ago, but with HiNET everything takes forever.

So far we've done SIN and we've scheduled TOK. We will take care of HKG "right after".
You can find more details at this URL: https://jira.pccwglobal.com/browse/PEER-443

column1508:
During planned maintenance activity for our PoP in Osaka the PCCWG services in Tokio were affected as well.
 
After thorough investigation from the PCCW Global Engineering team, it was found that services in Tokio were affected by a misconfiguration due to human error. In detail, at the beginning of the maintenance the on duty engineer had to deactivate ISIS IGP Protocol on specific router interfaces. This would allow transit traffic from Tokio through Osaka to smoothly switch over other available backbone links.  Instead of this, the Engineer deactivated by accident the ISIS instance from the whole router in Tokio resulting in International links routing failure.
column1599: The Network engineer assigned to investigate further the incident found the misconfiguration & immediately applied the correct setup.

Hello Cliff,

 

It appears you tried to establish a multi-hop eBGP IPv6 peering session with 2406:e500::1. But br02.hkg15 learns the prefix (2406:e500::1) via 6PE . Correct me if I am wrong.

In that case, this is an expected behaviour on IOS-XR. Since the next hop for 6PE prefix is placed in table for IPv4 while BGP looks for next hop to endpoint in table for IPv6. Hi Cliff,

 

We have reproduced this issue in the lab. Below is the summary of the lab test findings. Please note that all tests and debugs are executed in the lab, and the same hostname/IPv6 address was used for the sake of easy understanding.

 

1.When ASR9K/XR 5.3.3 tries to initiate a TCP BGP session to remote neighbours, a BGP check for the next-hop is mandatory to be carried out. If the corresponding route to multi-hop neighbour is learned via 6PE, ASR9K/XR 5.3.3 will report the message below and stop the negotiation of TCP BGP session due to “no route”, which is consistent with what you observed in production network.

_P/0/0/CPU0:br02.hkg15#_

 # In fact, once the BGP session is established, ASR9K will use BGP keepalive to detect BGP neighbour and verify next-hop reachability. In this case, even though the IPv6 static router is removed, the BGP session should be up because the 2 x BGP neighbour can be still reached each other via 6PE network. which is also consistent with what you observed in production network.

We do have ARIN/US-Based IPv4 addresses that can add up to a /20.
So the /20 would be a non-contiguous block of IPv4 ranges (like /21, /22s) which will eventually add up to a /20 as we do not have a single contiguous /20 IPv4 block.
 
Also, it goes without saying, reselling a /20 IPv4 block in today’s market where the internet is basically depleted of all IPv4 addresses, 1) we need to make sure we charge the customer an arm and a leg for these Ipv4 addresses and 2) obviously we need a few SMT approvals per the process which Philip and Anthony are well aware of.
 
Sorry for the delayed response, but IPv4 addresses is not something we want to be giving out with significant gain to PCCW.

Also, keep in mind these are ARIN/US-Based IP’s, so customer must be well aware so that they don’t start whining about Geo-IP Location issues later on.

Regards,
Sandeep

Hello Jean, Jacky, Sandeep



As you can see from the emails below, we have a bit of a situation at the 
ATH POP with the current setup.



Problem Statement:



•         We have a VIP customer (YAHSAT VPLS) who are subscribed to our 
Premium Support as well. They have a few links on this setup ranging from 
500M to 1Gig.

•         For the past few weeks, the 10G BB between VAR05.ATH01 – TE1/3/0 
and CR01.FRF02 (EP5365) has been unstable and I noticed yesterday that when 
this BB goes down, traffic is then routed on the 200M towards CR01.FRF05 but 
return traffic comes through VAR06.ATH01. For the L2VPNs, I could do a TE 
Tunnel to make the traffic symmetric but this issue affects some L3 
customers as well.

•         The two BB links at VAR05.ATH01, the 10G and 200M have equal ISIS 
metrics and I’m wondering if we could perhaps make it slightly worse on the 
200M so that it gets used as last resort if both 10Gs at var05 and VAR06 are 
out of service.






VAR05.ATH01 – Gig0/0/3 (During BB Flaps)








VAR05.ATH01 – Gig1/0/0 (During Flaps)








VAR05.ATH01 – TE1/3/0









Proposed Solution:



•         In addition to the above suggestion of changing the metric on the 
200M at VAR05, increase the capacity between the 2 PE’s by activating a 10G 
DISTRIB link. Both PE’s have 10G ports available



Please let me know if this the best way to go or propose a different 
solution.



Kind Regards



Solly Mathebula

Feb 12, 2020 22:25;635a238a928dc277b90528da;Hi [~accountid:5bbc909a707d880e51eefc7d] [~accountid:59f78fce068cd6328f465a66]

Looking at the list published by Wilfrid, it would be suicidal to filter our own IPs from peers because 1) the list is huge and not manageable and 2) not scalable and cannot be controlled because we will always assign our own IPv4 blocks to customers that want and pay for our IPv4 addresses and use BGP to advertise our blocks to PCCWG and their other upstream providers.

Blocking our own IP advertisements from other peers will kill connectivity to the customer from our network if the customer loses their connection to PCCWG and that is why in some ways we always had other measures like perimeter filtering with ACL161, loose uRPF (in the past), Arbor for checking DDOS attacks, blackhole filtering, etc in place.

I can understand filtering our prefixes from peers if they were statically assigned and/or if the customer was single-homed. We can't filter our own AS3491 IPv4/v6 blocks coming from peers because its dynamic and customers running BGP are multi-homed with other providers.

Regards,
Sandeep

column2121:
Feb 14, 2020 16:22;59f78fce068cd6328f465a66;Ajwani Sandeep,

I am just trying to get the best out of a complex situation.

I think there's 3 things we have to consider:
 * *Security*: We have to protect ourselves from hijacking. 
 * *Status quo*: We have randomly assigned IP blocks  to customers for years and we still do
 * *SAFE*: You have to do 1 thing at a time in a short period of time

Honestly, i don't feel confident with giving up with security. What if someone hijacks our address space and start receiving our own emails? I really don't want to take that blame.

And, at the same time, it's extremely hard to deal with the status quo.
I know, we could take a snapshot of what we have now, create a prefix-list that allows what's already assigned and rejects what's not. But what will happen when we assign a new prefix to our customers?

On paper we'd have to change the prefix-list once again. But how can we do that? Who's going to tell us and a new prefix was assigned and how? We don't have a workflow for that.

And if we want to define one then we need a Feature that can't been worked on any time sooner than next May. And even if we could make it very quick and do everything in 1 sprint (thing that i doubt), that would force us to put this Story on hold until early June.

At the same time we have our most VIPs customers (Netvigator, Facebook and Amazon) waiting for it. Business owners have assigned a value of 9 to this Story and thus i believe it is rather important to deliver it as soon as we can.

All that said i think we have to take make tradeoffs and deliver what SAFE calls a MVP which is something that is good enough although not perfect, but can be improved over time

And I believe my proposal is good enough (because the status quo proves it) and leaves enough room for improvements.

Please let me know your comments

Thank you

Regards

 Dear Petros,

 Please swap the optic from VAR01.BUH01 Gi0/0/1/0 to SW01.BUH01 Gi0/0/19 in Rack 5, the remote hands procedure are as follows:
 * Disconnect and label the UTP cable connect to VAR01.BUH01 Gi0/0/1/0
 * Disconnect and label the SMF fibre connect to SW01.BUH01 Gi0/0/19
 * Remove the GLC-T-CURV from VAR01.BUH01 Gi0/0/1/0
 * Remove the GLC-LH-SMD from SW01.BUH01 Gi0/0/19
 * Re-insert GLC-T-CURV to SW01.BUH01 Gi0/0/19 and re-connect the UTP cable from step 1
 * Re-insert GLC-T-CURV to VAR01.BUH01 Gi0/0/1/0 and re-connect the SMF fibre from step 2
 * Re-label the UTP cable and SMF fibre patching

 

After swapping, you can use SW01.BUH01 Gi0/0/19 [Rack 5 DDF-1 Port 1 UTP RJ45] for the console customer. Thanks.

column2089:
Feb 12, 2020 01:45;59f78fce068cd6328f465a66;[~accountid:635a238a928dc277b90528da],

Thanks for your reply.

I agree with you it's a little bit confusing, but the reason is it's just an intermediate step toward the final goal. Anyway we will publish that file on RIPE as soon as the new route-policies will be deployed (Roughly during next PI).

Since Amazon was asking for it, we've designed the communities to implement the very same feature either for V4 and V6.

The new communities to identify customers, peers and self-originated routes are needed to make the outbound policies simpler and, at the same time, more robust.

For instance the below looks complicated:
{noformat}
!
route-policy Pass-AS3491-and-Customers-North-America-OUT
  if not (community matches-any Customers-North-America or community matches-any Customers-V6 or as-path is-local) then
    drop
  endif
end-policy
!
{noformat}
 

With the types we can simplify the above as follow:
{noformat}
!
route-policy Pass-AS3491-and-Customers-North-America-OUT
  if community matches-any Route-Type-Customer and community matches-any Route-Type-North-America then
    done
  endif
  drop
end-policy
!
{noformat}
It's much easier to read and it enforces a default drop at the end.

Regarding North-America, [~accountid:5bbc909a707d880e51eefc7d] has suggested that from customers' and peers' standpoint 65001 and 65002 are the same region.

I will fix the type for 3491:9096.

Please tell me more about Africa Express

Jan 19, 2020 01:36;615b54e3c7bea400692dc947;Dear [~accountid:635a238a928dc277b90528da],

We have some constraints on IOS Upgrade at this moment.

Current environment:
1. the backbone between var04.mpm01 and var02.mtu01 [MPT(PCG)-MTZ(PCG) EP3162] is ready.
2. the backbone between var01.jnb02 and var01.mtu01 [JNB(PCG)-MTZ(PCG) EP3161] is not ready yet.
3. MRV, which is used to connect to the console port of mtu01's devices, has inband connection only. Also it is connected to sw02.mtu01 physically.

In short, MRV's inband connection is riding on [MPT(PCG)-MTZ(PCG) EP3162] only.


Here are constraints on IOS Upgrade.

1. We can upgrade var01.mtu01 and sw01.mtu01 under current environment.

2. We cannot upgrade var02.mtu01 as the upgrade will disconnect [MPT(PCG)-MTZ(PCG) EP3162]. Console connection to each mtu01s' devices will be dropped. As var02.mtu01 and var01.mtu01 are ASR9001 and using IOS-XR 4.3.4 and IOS-XR 5.3.3 respectively, we need to use TURBOBOOT to upgrade them via console. When [JNB(PCG)-MTZ(PCG) EP3161] is ready, we could upgrade var02.mtu01 because I have configured that we could access MRV via either var02.mtu01 or var01.mtu01.

3. We could upgrade sw02.mtu01, however there is a risk that we could not access MRV if the upgrade is failed.

Hi Max,

Thank you for your patience. The BU is on Christmas and New Year holidays, the reaction from them will be slow.

1

The LOOPBACK DIAG packets from the line card CPU to NP is a health check mechanism. Every minute a DIAGS packet per NP is injected from the LC CPU, to the Punt Switch, and all are looped back at the NP's. They do NOT go to the fabric at all. Diagnostic packets are sent every minute by default. The failure message if one is lost 3 times in a row is shown here.
 * Diag send path: LC:online diags -> Inject -> LC-NP -> (loop)
 * Diag return path: LC-NP -> Punt -> online diags:LC

|LC/0/0/CPU0:Dec 24 09:26:40.392 : pfm_node_lc[304]: %PLATFORM-DIAGS-0-LC_NP_LOOPBACK_FAILED_TX_PATH : Set\|online_diag_lc[172118]\|Line card NPU loopback Test(0x2000006)\|link failure mask is *0x3*.|

This message has a link failure mask.

 

Usually, if a reload doesn’t fix the LC_NP_LOOPBACK_FAILED_TX_PATH error, we need to replace it. Please let me know if you want to do this.

Slot 0/1/CPU0 auto reload due to NP0 Persistent Initialization Failure.

1.After checking all the information,slot 0/1/CPU0 NP failed to initialization with multiple process crash.

Slot 0/1/CPU0 auto reload due to NP0 Persistent Initialization Failure.

 

*Problem Analysis:*

1.After checking all the information,slot 0/1/CPU0 NP failed to initialization with multiple process crash.

Analyze:

From above information, we could know this issue is started from 21:28:22.

21:28:22: BGP and ISIS down on cr02.ash02 and var01.rdu01.

21:28:22-22:33:27: as BGP and ISIS down, so there is no traffic on the link during this time, and ARP entry not timeout on cr02.ash02, so there is no resolution request generate.

22:33:27: ARP entry should be timeout on cr02.ash02. Error log shows there is a local link loop of TenGigE0/3/0/0 on cr02.ash02, this should be caused by transmission.

22:33:27-23:32:34: the link loop continue happened during this time and ARP resolution failed on cr02.ash02 due to the loop.

23:32:34: Local link loop issue might solved as cr02.ash02 could send out ARP resolution request but didn’t receive reply.

23:32:34-01:09:22: cr02.ash02 continue send out ARP resolution request but could not get reply.

01:09:22: After link up/down issue happened on var01.rdu01, cr02.ash02 could receive the ARP reply, but could not confirm if the ARP entries are normal on var01.rdu01 or not.

01:09:22-01:56:42: As the ARP resolution success on cr02.ash02, but routing protocol still didn’t up, here might be still a connectivity issue, such as var01.rdu01 still didn’t have ARP entries.

01:56:42: After reload card 0/0 of var01.rdu01, ARP issue should be solved then ISIS and BGP come up.

 

And the information showed that cr02.ash02 could send out ARP request when 00:48 which reported by customer.

Also cr02.ash02 receive the ARP reply after link up/down on var01.rdu01 when 01:09:22.

But we didn’t know var01.rdu01 could send out ARP request normally or not due to the reload..

 

So this issue might be caused by transit device that dropped the ARP packets and routing protocol packets.

Or another possible reason is ASR9901 didn’t send out the ARP request(dropped ARP reply/request packets).

So now we need to first focus on ASR9901, to confirm if it successful send out ARP request or dropped packets.

 

Below is the forwarding path in internal of ASR9K:

Packet path for ARP request:

ARP -> SPP (LC) -> Punt_Switch (LC) -> NP -> Wire

Packet path for ARP reply:

Wire -> NP -> Punt_Switch  (LC) -> SPP (LC) -> ARP

 

For confirm the packets is dropped on which component of ASR9K, we need verify below 4 parts:
 # Verify whether packets are entering/leaving the ARP Application at CPU.
 # Verify whether packets are entering/leaving the SPP
 # Verify whether packets are entering/leaving interface
 # Verify whether packets are dropped at NP

This Syslog indicates that we also ran out of FEC ID as the rest of the warnings, it’s like a confirmation. We can’t recover without an LC reload or in some lucky cases “clear cef location <LC>”

 

Keep in mind that:

In per prefix mode, each l3vpn prefix will use a FEC.

In per-vrf mode, all the prefixes in the vrf will share a fec for the same pair of nexthops.

If you are using ecmp paths for per-prefix then you are limited by 4K ecmp fec.

Eric, Michael,

We have deployed 2 NCS55A-36H-SE routers (br04.hkg12 and clbr01.tok02) and as you know we plan to deploy more in the near future.

 

For Premium GIA services on BR routers, we have activated address-families IPv4, IPv6, VPNv4 and VPNv6.


What do we need to do to reduce the ecmp fec usage as we are not hitting this on br04.hkg12 (71%) yet versus clbr01.tok02 (is maxed out at 100%).

 

Regards,

Sandeep Ajwani 

AVP, Engineering

*Subject:* Re: SR 687998181 : PCCW:NCS-55A1-36HS-SYS--PLATFORM-PLAT_FIB-3-HW_PROG_ERROR error log

 

Hello Sandeep,

 

Sorry for the belated response. Finally we have an update from TAC/BU. Please check the detailed information below.

Due to NCS55A1 card limitation, this only allows 2048x2 ECMP prefixes, and we have checked the ip route for br04.hkg12 and clbr01.tok02, below is the ECMP route summary for both NCS55A1.

 
|Node|ECMP route|
|br04.hkg12|1460|
|clbr01.tok02|5332|

 

So the usage for br04.hkg12 is :1460*2/4096=71%

So the usage for clbr01.tok02 is:  over than 4K limitation, =100%

And you can use the command ‘_show controllers npu resources ecmpfec location 0/0/cpu0_’ to see the current usage.

 

To reduce the usage of ecmp_fec of NCS55A1, there is a workaround provided by TAC/BU team as below,

Workaround: configuring LDP label filtering on br04.hkg12 and clbr01.tok02, note that once configured, "clear route ipv4 unicast "is required to take effect.

 

_ipv4 prefix-list Global-LSP-Filter_

_10 permit 66.0.0.0/8 ge 32                 >>>this IP range is just an example to assign the MPLS label for host route /32, which is the IPv4 address of loopback0 of each router in MPLS Core. PCCWGlobal may configure the corresponding IP range for MPLS Core Network._

 __ 

_mpls ldp_

_nsr_

_graceful-restart_

_router-id 66.1.1.1_

_address-family ipv4_

  _discovery targeted-hello accept_

  _label_

   _local_

    _allocate for Global-LSP-Filter_

    _advertise_

     _explicit-null_

    _!_

   _!_

   _remote_

    _accept_

     _from 66.2.2.2:0 for Global-LSP-Filter          >>> this IP address is just an example, PCCWGlobal may configure the IPv4 address of Loopback 0 of the upstream core router._

     _from 66.3.3.3:0 for Global-LSP-Filter          >>> this IP address is just an example, PCCWGlobal may configure the IPv4 address of Loopback 0 of the upstream core router_

 

From my understanding, 2 x NCS55A1 routers have not carried the production traffic and served as BR yet. Correct me if I am wrong. Could you please apply the configuration to br04.hkg12 and clbr01.tok02 and use the command ‘_show controllers npu resources ecmpfec location 0/0/cpu0_’ to check the usage of ecmp_fec. Simultaneously, it’s necessary to check if the new error log is triggered as before.

 

To be honest, the workaround above is to address the current issue only. We still need some time to study how to save the HW resource in MPLS VPN scenario. We will keep you posted once we have solid the conclusion. Thank you for your understanding and support.

 

Regards,

Michael

After escalation, there were some discussions and online troubleshooting with TAC/BU engineers on this case, and they are clear about the NC5K setup w/o VRF in PCCWG network . Currently, they still are testing in the lab and verifying the workaround for this case. I personally think we need some time to sync up internally tomorrow morning. Hence, we may update you on this case with the finding and recommendation by the EOD tomorrow. Please let me know if you have any concerns.

 

Regards,

Michael

 

*From:* Sandeep Ajwani <[sajwani@pccwglobal.com|mailto:sajwani@pccwglobal.com]>

*Subject:* Re: SR 687998181 : PCCW:NCS-55A1-36HS-SYS--PLATFORM-PLAT_FIB-3-HW_PROG_ERROR error log

 

Thanks Michael.


But also do keep in mind the VPNv4 and VPNv6 prefixes received from the GIA RR’s on these NCS55A1 BR routers which basically are receiving the CT/CU VRF routes, Google/Netvigator VRFs routes, etc from the RRs.

 

Also, take a look at the EBGP session between 65004 and 65002 like I mentioned below for the CT/CU routes received from US PE/BR routers (br04.sjo01 and br03.lax05) on those NCS55A1 BR routers.

 

Thanks but please make this 1^st^ priority task to work internally with the TAC/BU team closely next Monday.

Sandeep Ajwani

Hello Sandeep,

 

Regarding the reply from TAC engineer, I totally agree with what you said indeed.  First of all, the VRFs of clbr01.tok02 and br02.hkg12 haven’t been enabled so far. Hence, from my understanding, 4K entries in the ‘ecmp_fec’ would not be consumed in this case.

In fact, we have compared the IGP routing-table between clbr01.tok02 and br02.hkg12, the difference is the amount of ECMP IGP prefix, and also I think we have verified a possible workaround  to reduce the entry of ecmp fec in the lab. As mentioned in my previous email, we really need to work with TAC/BU team so that we could provide a workable and stable solution to eliminate the risk for NCS5K.  

It’s weekend but I will consider this as a 1^s t^ priority task and work with the internal team closely next Monday. Thank you for your understanding.

 

Regards,

Michael

To ease the congestion on the b2b links between cr01.tap06-br01.tap06, a new 10GE distribution link is ready to be turned up.

However, instead of putting a new /30 on this 10GE b2b link, kindly work on establishing a 110G LAG [11x10GE] between cr01.tap06-br01.tap06.

To ensure this change is transparent, please create a BE interface at both ends, add this new 10GE link to the Bundle and assign a new /30 link to the BE interface.

Bring up ISIS, RSVP, MPLS-TE and MPLS LDP on the BE interface with this new 10GE link.
Once everything is up, move each of the existing 10GE b2b links to the Bundle thereby increasing the bandwidth on the Bundle starting from 10Gbps to 110Gbps.

After the 110G LAG is up and working fine, you can work on removing the individual 10GE links from ISIS, RSVP, MPLS-TE and MPLS LDP on both sides.

Kindly prepare the MOP and please forward with the turn up today, including submitting the rDNS ticket, etc.

Regards,

Dec 06, 2019 11:20;635a238a928dc277b90528da;Dear [~accountid:615b4fa9c669a600695da155]
Kindly follow the turn up process of new routers as outlined on the wiki link https://wiki.pccwglobal.com/display/INA/How+To+Turn-up+new+routers

Enclosed are the IPs assigned for cr06.ldn01 and please watch the approach and feedback from the different engineers below before moving forward.

Hello [~accountid:637dc5219960988ef6bdbff6]

Kindly help to submit the DNS forward and reverse IDI tickets and likewise the ACS/ISE IPS request tickets and link them to this ticket.

Dear [~accountid:637dc4c49341d1f1360564e0]

Kindly help to update IPAM with the IP addresses for cr06.ldn01.

Please take a quick look at the PI as CR06.LDN01 is a Core router but it is the first NCS55A1 device to be used as a Core router.

Could you kindly provide or guide Gary to the Configuration templates on Samba for the ASR9K as a Core router and the NCS55A1 as a BR router. After we have brought up cr06.ldn01, you can make another configuration template for the NCS55A1 as a CR router.

6.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway (see above IP table 207.176.48.190)

[https://community.cisco.com/t5/switching/inactive-interface-on-ws-c4507r-e/td-p/2055797]
Limitation and Restriction on Supervisor Engine 7-E and Supervisor Engine 7L-E
Please note the following:
• When you use WS-X45-SUP-7-E in RPR or SSO mode, only the first two uplinks on each supervisor
engine are available. The second two uplinks are unavailable.

column1508: lldp_mgr is the sole verifier for global lldp config. Suspect seem to be a case of racing condition wherein lldp_mgr process(running in active RP) has exited on global lldp unconfig. But sysmgr (which is responsible for spawing all the processes in the device) is unaware of the same. As a result, during the next reconfig of global lldp config, sysmgr presumes that lldp_mgr process is still running and does not spawn the same. As a result there is no verifier for global lldp config causing this verification error.

Hi Octavio,
 
Below was analysis from Dev team:
 
RCA
=====
lldp_mgr is the sole verifier for global lldp config. Suspect seem to be a case of racing condition wherein lldp_mgr process(running in active RP) has exited on global lldp unconfig. But sysmgr (which is responsible for spawing all the processes in the device) is unaware of the same. As a result, during the next reconfig of global lldp config, sysmgr presumes that lldp_mgr process is still running and does not spawn the same. As a result there is no verifier for global lldp config causing this verification error.

Nov 05, 2019 22:46;635a238a928dc277b90528da;Dear [~accountid:615b54e3c7bea400692dc947]

Good work on the preliminary testing and attempt at finding free /30 IPv4 space at HKG05 which is difficult even after having 2 management /24 blocks - 63.218.144.0/24 and 63.218.214.0/24.

The important point you should be aware of when turning up Trans-Pac backbone links is as you know to provide direct Asia-Europe connectivity to MPLS and EE customers, you will see those explicit-paths a lot of exclude-address in all the VAR-VAR routers like below

ip explicit-path name HK-SMW5 enable
exclude-address 63.223.41.73
 exclude-address 63.223.41.77
 exclude-address 63.223.42.1
 exclude-address 63.223.42.5

Basically,these exclude address are IPv4 addresses of all Asia-US / Trans-Pac backbone links to force Asia-Europe traffic for MPLS customers via the direct path instead of via US.

Therefore, as HKG05-SJO01 is a Trans-Pac 10GE backbone circuit, we must use one of the pre-assigned IPv4 blocks in the IPv4 sheet like below.

63.223.41.0/24	For PCCW Global (TOK01) - To be used for Trans-Pac backbone links to TOK ONLY

63.223.42.0/24	For PCCW Global (HKG15) - To be used for Trans-Pac Backbone Links to HKG and TOK ONLY

Therefore, for this case I assigned the subnet 63.223.42.44/30 in the IPv4 sheet and you can see it under Fully Migrated tab.

Please use this /30 for the HKG05-SJO01 10GE backbone MOP.

TenGE0-0-0-1.cr06.hkg05.pccwbtn.net.	63.223.42.45
TenGE0-2-0-9.cr06.sjo01.pccwbtn.net.	63.223.42.46

The Bundle default hash way is base on the src-dst-mac. Mac address will modify by the up/down stream.
Could we change to the src-dst-ip by use below configuration:
 
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:A9K-BNG#configure
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:A9K-BNG(config)#l2vpn
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:A9K-BNG(config-l2vpn)#load-balancing flow ?
  src-dst-ip   Use source and destination IP addresses for hashing
  src-dst-mac  Use source and destination MAC addresses for hashing
 
l2vpn
    load-balancing flow src-dst-mac
This is the default configuration, and will cause the NP to build the flow label from the source and destination MAC addresses in each frame.
 
l2vpn
    load-balancing flow src-dst-ip
This is the recommended configuration, and will cause the NP to build the flow label from the source and destination IP addresses in each frame.
 
Could you do modify to the src-det-ip and let me know the result?

Please help raise remote hand to configure the iDRAC  for ipesvr01.mrs01.

|Server Name|Server Port|iDRAC IP Address|Subet Mask|Gateway IP|
|ipesvr01.mrs01|iDRAC|63.222.61.254|255.255.255.240|63.222.61.241|

Here is steps to configure network for iDRAC port:
1. Connect keyboard and monitor to IPESVR01.MRS01
2. Turn on the Dell machine (IPESVR01.MRS01)
3. Press <F2> during Power-on Self-test (POST)
4. In the System Setup Main Menu page, click iDRAC Settings, the iDRAC Settings page is displayed
5. Click Network, the Network page is displayed
6. Specify the network settings (please see below IP address)
6.1 In Network Settings -> Enable NIC -> select the Enabled option
6.1.1 From the NIC Selection drop-down menu, select the Dedicated
6.2 In IPV4 Settings -> Enable IPv4 -> select the Disable DHCP option
6.2.1 Fill in the static IP Address (see above IP table 63.222.61.254)
6.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway (see above IP table 63.222.61.241)
6.2.3 Fill in the static Subnet Mak (see above IP table 255.255.255.240)
7. Click Back, click Finish, and then click Yes. The network information is saved and the system reboot.

column1: 2019 Internal Pentest Remediation Action: Insecure TCP Service: Server Using SSH Protocol Version 1
column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
Hi [~accountid:5f2be5fb2aa2500028cf3bc4]

Following the recently concluded Penetration test, 

63.223.29.210

63.223.29.206

63.223.29.202

were identified to be vulnerable to an attack and needs to be remediated as soon as possible. Below is the detail of the identified vulnerability and recommended remediation action.

*Insecure TCP Service: Server Using SSH Protocol Version 1* 

*Impact:*

An attacker could potentially both inject into and read the contents of any transmission using SSH version 1. This protocol is susceptible to a number of security vulnerabilities, which originate from both implementation and design flaws. The protocol is not cryptographically secure, enabling an attacker to break the transient SSH version 1 server key responsible for the negotiation of session encryption parameters. The various implementation flaws could lead to a complete compromise of the server.

*Recommended Action:*  

Recommendation is that the SSH daemon is configured to support version 2 only. To implement this, locate the ‘Protocol’ directive in the SSH daemon configuration file (usually ‘sshd_conf’) and replace the current setting with: Protocol 2

Sep 27, 2019 17:56;637dc55c77acd224b33e37b7;Hello Muach,

Frankly, without detailed logs/show output/topology, it’s hard for us to pin-point the possible cause.
If the issue re-occurred, the recommended commands below can be used to capture the useful information for further investigation.

show clock
show logging
show run interface tunnel X
show crypto isakmp sa
show crypto ipsec sa peer IP
show tunnel endpoint tunnel X
show dmvpn
show dmvpn details
show ip nhrp
show ip nhrp nhs >>>on spoke
show ip nhrp tunnel X     >>>on hub
show ip nhrp multicast   >>>on hub

Furthermore, I suggest you open a TAC case to follow up the similar issue in future.

Regards,
Michael

Good morning Engineering team, 
 
We are facing an issue on this interface : 
 
br05.hkg05# int Be10.91
 
Where the IPV6 adjacency does not work properly.
 
The IPV6 of the customer is no pingable when the bundle is complete and both interfaces are UP :
 
Hu0/1/0/1
Hu0/4/0/0
 
As soon as I shutdown one of the interfaces, then the adjacency is complete and I can ping the IPV6 neighbour without errors.
 
I have checked the ND logs : 
 
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:br05.hkg05#sh ipv6 neighbors Bundle-Ether10.91
Wed Sep 18 10:03:19.297 GMT

Aug 13 15:05:15.529 nd/error 0/RSP0/CPU0 t1  ifh: Bundle-Ether10.91 (0x80009a0)  MPLS config disabled
Aug 13 15:05:15.555 nd/error 0/RSP0/CPU0 t1  ifh=Bundle-Ether10.91 (0x80009a0) , RA not started, error:'ipv6-nd' detected the 'warning' condition 'RA not started, not supported'(0x42ec9e00)
Aug 13 15:05:17.559 nd/error 0/RSP0/CPU0 t1  ifh=Bundle-Ether10.91 (0x80009a0) , RA not started, error:'ipv6-nd' detected the 'warning' condition 'RA not started, not supported'(0x42ec9e00)
 
Sep 19 10:47:48.745 nd/error 0/RSP0/CPU0 t1  VIMI update Bundle-Ether10 (0x80002e0) , update master failed (No such file or directory)
Sep 19 10:47:48.745 nd/error 0/RSP0/CPU0 t1  VIMI update Bundle-Ether10.86 (0x80003a2) , update master failed (No such file or directory)
 
I have compared the configuration of the bundling with other interfaces of the same type and saw no difference.
 
I have spoken to the customer to try and see if there was any active equipment on the path that could block the adjacency (ie a swich that would block multicast). Apparently there was a type of switch on the path (I am still not sure as I do not speak Chinese), and the customer has removed it.
 
But the issue is still present. 
At the moment the customer has shut the interface Hu0/4/0/0 and the ping is OK and the BGP session is stable.
But as soon as he enables both interfaces then the IPV6 does not work anymore. 
 
Can you assist on this ?
 
I have attached in this email the history of this ticket for your reference.
 
Regards.

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Sep 17 09:22:53.923 : SSHD_[65737]: %SECURITY-SSHD-6-INFO_GENERAL : Failed to read from socket :Connection reset by peer
RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Sep 17 09:22:53.923 : SSHD_[65737]: %SECURITY-SSHD-6-INFO_GENERAL : Failed to read from socket :Connection reset by peer
 
Take *“Failed to set window size”* as example:
Cisco XR code by design accepts request for a terminal window size less than 512. If the application request for more than a window size of 512 then this message is displayed. The message indicates this is a fatal condition but this is NOT business impacting and it will just resize the terminal size window.
This error comes in when the client is connecting to the ASR9k and setting a width that is not within the range allowed on the router. Once client tries to set this value upon connecting ASR9k ignores as its out of range and populates the error message. The client should still be able to access the router.  If you find the "Setting window size" to be greater than 512 you should try to change the setting on client.
 
------------------------------------------------------------------
There are 3 possibilities in which the message *“Too many console line state change interrupts”* is printed by devc-conaux.
1. Cable is loose
2. Port is at fault
3. Cable is at fault
 
If any of the above case is there, devc-conaux will receive too many interrupts to handle and will print the message. Also it will start hogging the CPU since it has
to do a lot of work to process the interrupts. By this time wdsysmon will kick in and do a switchover to recover, but as you are using a ASR9001, there is no supervisor redundancy.
So please help to check above or replace cables.
 
Pls feel free to contact me regarding on this issue !
 
Best Regards,
Fangting Nan

5.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway (63.222.77.1)
5.2.3 Fill in the static Subnet Mak (255.255.255.240)

6. Click Back, click Finish, and then click Yes. The network information is saved and the system reboots

Enclosed please find the doc Setup iDRAC.pdf for detail steps.

Regards,
Jacky

Here is steps to configure network for iDRAC port:
1. Connect keyboard and monitor to IPESVR01.MEX02
2. Turn on the Dell machine (IPESVR01.MEX02)
3. Press <F2> during Power-on Self-test (POST)
4. In the System Setup Main Menu page, click iDRAC Settings, the iDRAC Settings page is displayed
5. Click Network, the Network page is displayed
6. Specify the network settings (please see below IP address)
6.1 In Network Settings -> Enable NIC -> select the Enabled option
6.1.1 From the NIC Selection drop-down menu, select the Dedicated
6.2 In IPV4 Settings -> Enable IPv4 -> select the Disable DHCP option
6.2.1 Fill in the static IP Address (see above IP table 63.222.89.30)
6.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway (see above IP table 63.222.89.17)
6.2.3 Fill in the static Subnet Mak (see above IP table 255.255.255.240)
7. Click Back, click Finish, and then click Yes. The network information is saved and the system reboot.

Oct 21, 2019 16:02;615b3e9cc5388b00696ca529;Hi [~accountid:615b54e3c7bea400692dc947], [~accountid:637dc4c49341d1f1360564e0], CAS01 is an African POP which could be connected to another African POP one day.

So far CAS01 is connected to EU(LDN12 and PAR04), so isis metric 200 and TE metric 100 are fine.

But if CAS01 is connected to another African POP, we need to avoid  the case that the CAS01 POP does attract all the traffic between EU and Africa. 
Then the metrics should be changed according to the following formula for isis metric *{color:#172b4d}between CAS01 and EU{color}* :     EU-Africa = 10000+latency*100, 
CAS01-Africa = latency*100,

LDN12-CAS01:10000+44ms*100=14400, no TE metrics required as MRS01 is very close so the traffic from/to Asia
                                                                   should go through EU.
PAR04-CAS01:10000+51ms*100=15100, {color:#172b4d}no TE metrics required as MRS01 is very close so the traffic from/to Asia{color}
{color:#172b4d}                                                                   should go through EU.{color}

Of course I'll review them before the change. Thanks.

6.1.1 From the NIC Selection drop-down menu, select the Dedicated
6.2 In IPV4 Settings -> Enable IPv4 -> select the Disable DHCP option
6.2.1 Fill in the static IP Address (see above IP table 63.222.35.14)
6.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway (see above IP table 63.222.35.1)
6.2.3 Fill in the static Subnet Mak (see above IP table 255.255.255.240)
7. Click Back, click Finish, and then click Yes. The network information is saved and the system reboot

So, please help to withdraw the Alibaba SC routes to those PCCW Global sister companies (e.g. 4515,...)  in HK IX. 

Thanks.

ASR920 hit bug CSCvk35460.

The symptom of bug CSCvk35460 is that When ASR920 is running for nearly 889 days, Interface link states are frozen.  Changes to link state (up/down) will not be reflected in the 'show interface' output.  New  interfaces being plugged in will not come up. The bug is matched for our issue for three reasons.
a)     The issue router's uptime is all nearly 889 days.
sw02.tok13 uptime is 2 years, 22 weeks, 1 day, 15 hours, 23 minutes
sw05.tok01 uptime is 2 years, 23 weeks, 4 days, 23 hours, 56 minutes
b)    the trigger is that the router link is down before due to site outage and cannot up again, which cause the link status frozen to down.
c)     And do the hard loop test the link is not up either, but the LED is green, and reload will solve the issue, which is match the similar case we found hit this bug.

Hi Eric,
 
Thank you for your support.
 
Hi Max,
 
Yes, at this point, we suspect we are hitting the bug CSCvk35460. This bug is not customer visible, so I will share some information of this bug here.
The symptom of bug CSCvk35460 is that When ASR920 is running for nearly 889 days, Interface link states are frozen.  Changes to link state (up/down) will not be reflected in the 'show interface' output.  New  interfaces being plugged in will not come up. The bug is matched for our issue for three reasons.
a)     The issue router's uptime is all nearly 889 days.
*sw02.tok13 uptime is 2 years, 22 weeks, 1 day, 15 hours, 23 minutes*
*sw05.tok01 uptime is 2 years, 23 weeks, 4 days, 23 hours, 56 minutes*
b)    the trigger is that the router link is down before due to site outage and cannot up again, which cause the link status frozen to down.
c)     And do the hard loop test the link is not up either, but the LED is green, and reload will solve the issue, which is match the similar case we found hit this bug.
Suggest to have an IOS upgrade as Eric recommendation to fix the bug.
Thank you.

Jun 14 12:18:30.784 bundlemgr/local/fast 0/2/CPU0 t3  PKTIO RX: Handled timer expiry on port TenGigE0/2/0/7 (0x04000280) with ITDB port ID 4 <==

Jun 14, 2019 22:42;637dc4f1a593cb822e9419f7;Jean,
It appears that the "Add Prefix" feature was used to add the supernet into the db at 16:50 on June 13. The first time the automated code detected the announcement was at 17:30 on June 13. Since the automated system already found the prefix in its data store it assumed it was already pushed to the router.
There should have been an automatic push of the filter into the router after the Add Prefix was triggered but that may have failed.
There is a manual Push Filter function in the WEB interface that can be used force an update in events such as this.

Hi Ted,

 
 * There is no QoS on the 10G link between var05.frf02 and cr01.frf05 but the usage is around 2% of the 10G.

Var05.frf02 is used as IPSEC Gateway, so CE team creates GRE and IPSec tunnels with QoS.

Apparently, QoS on the physical interface is not supported by the cisco device if QoS is used on GRE or IPSec Tunnels using the physical interface, like on other PE’s used as IPSec gateway in our network.

The output drops we see on var05.frf02 Ten0/3/0 are caused by GRE/IPSec Tunnels on var05.frf02, to get rid of them, CE team has to use child policy to upper queue limit on each Tunnel as per cisco support.

 
 * DUB03 side, I don’t see any drop on PE – CE in DUB03 in this email thread.

 
 * The queue limit for Bronze and Silver classes on NP7186 have been upped last Thursday May 30 17:14:48 2019 UTC (3 days, 16 hours ago).

Silver queue-limit is now 2000ms instead of 900ms.

Bronze queue-limit is now 4000ms instead of 2000ms.

So far DXB(PCG) IP003186 is no more suffering of packet loss.

Note the PMAP core-queuing-eng is also used on interface POS0/3/0/0 STM1 NP9132 connected to var01.dub02.

The packet loss reported by the IPCE tool on cr01.ldn12 pos0/3/0/0  affecting the Bronze class could have been fixed, AUH(PCG) IP003187 is on var01.dub02.

 
 * dub03 has 2 Up-Links to cr01.dub03, 1 GigE link(to be preferred) and 1 SDH STM1 link used as second/backup Up-Link.

For some unknown reason the TE-Tunnel1040 to var01.dub03 on var05.frf02 was still using the SDH STM1 link between cr01.dub03 and var01.dub03.

We forced the traffic to use the GigE link on last Fri 31/May around 07:45UTC, now it is using the GigE link.

Doing below steps to fix the inconsistency, if previous not work, try next:

 

-- add a static route about x.x.x.x or clear route ipv4 unicast x.x.x.x to trigger a fib upgrade

-- shutdown/no shut the two inconsistent next hop interface

-- clear cef ipv4 linecard location 0/x/cpu0

-- reload the linecard

Akamai states that they cannot reach their destination IP (202.4.185.96) from one source IP (.39), but can from a similar IP (.37).  Our initial and follow up tests showed packet loss to the destination, which was learned from Sprint, so I sent this out for investigation.  However upon further discussion between TAC and the USNOC it was noticed that when the customer used the “bad” source IP it would stop directly at a certain PCCW HOP each and every time.    This HOP and IP (BR04.SJO01 / 63.223.60.106) were featured prominently, in the case that is attached, where another customer would hit 63.223.60.106 and stop.

May 14, 2019 15:46;712020:1c4de9a1-879b-434d-ac02-16ce22b36c58;*From:* Xuesong Jia (xuesjia) [[mailto:xuesjia@cisco.com]]
