*Subject:* Re: SR 686661832 : PCCW:ASR-9010-DC-V2-Troubleshooting

 

_++ Michael Ma from AS team_

 

Hi Max,

 

Hope you are doing well. I’d like to give you a quick update about this issue.

 

SW: 4.3.4

HW: ASR-9010-DC-V2 + A9K-RSP440-TR + A9K-2x100GE-TR

 

Problem Description:

IPv4 traffic problem from br02.hkg08 to 217.66.11.2 with below path:

 

br02.hkg08(63.216.156.221) ------ Routers ------ (Hu0/7/0/0)br04.sjo01(BE25) ------ Routers ------ Dst(217.66.11.2)

 

Action Taken:

1) When ping from 63.216.156.221 to 217.66.11.2, on Hu0/7/0/0 of br04.sjo01, ingress ACL could match. But egress ACL on BE 25 was not matched, which means packet has arrived Hu0/7/0/0, but not send out of BE25.

 

2) online trouble shooting find FIB update was abnormal on two A9K-2x100GE-TR Line card about prefix 217.66.11.2.

The route to 217.66.11.2 should be next hop Bundle-Ether25 and update on May  5 09:41:42.593: 

 

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:br04.sjo01#sh route 217.66.11.2 

Thu May  9 09:39:34.367 GMT

Routing entry for 217.66.10.0/23 

  Known via "bgp 65002", distance 20, metric 100

   Tag 174, type external

  Installed May  5 09:41:42.587 for 3d23h

  Routing Descriptor Blocks

    63.217.21.98, from 63.217.21.98, BGP external

      Route metric is 100 

  No advertising protos.

 

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:br04.sjo01#sh cef 217.66.11.2 detail 

Thu May  9 09:51:05.082 GMT

217.66.10.0/23, version 13809782590, internal 0x14000001 (ptr 0x76546244) [1], 0x0 (0x0), 0x0 (0x0) 

Updated May  5 09:41:42.593

<snip>

   via 63.217.21.98, 3 dependencies, recursive, bgp-ext [flags 0x6020]

    path-idx 0 [0x7ab5b744 0x0]

    next hop 63.217.21.98 via 63.217.21.98/32

Load distribution: 0 (refcount 1) 

    Hash  OK  Interface                 Address

    0     Y   Bundle-Ether25            63.217.21.98  

 

However, the fib programmed on 0/6 and 0/7 shows next hop is Bundle-Ether18.  And the fib has not been updated since Apr 29 13:01:40.707.

 

RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:br04.sjo01#sh cef 217.66.11.2 detail location 0/6/CPU0 

Thu May  9 09:51:52.467 GMT 

217.66.10.0/23, version 3811532109, internal 0x14000001 (ptr 0x93ef7adc) [1], 0x0 (0x0), 0x0 (0x0) 

Updated Apr 29 13:01:40.707 

<snip>

   via 63.218.7.102, 5 dependencies, recursive, bgp-ext [flags 0x6020]

    path-idx 0 [0x8e3a4c0c 0x0]

    next hop 63.218.7.102 via 63.218.7.102/32

Load distribution: 0 (refcount 1)

 

    Hash  OK  Interface                 Address

    0     Y   Bundle-Ether18            63.218.7.102  

 

3) the problem was resolved after reload the line card

 

4) we checked the show tech cef and cef trace, found cef on LC 0/6 and 0/7 are both work normally, no memory high issue.  

We also searched in database, so far could not find a bug firmly match this issue.  

 

Analysis:

In XR forwarding mechanism, would have below steps when a ipv4 unicast route update happens:

RIB Update(*show route x.x.x.x detail*)  ---> FIB Update(*show cef x.x.x.x detail* )---> FIB Update on Line Card(*show cef x.x.x.x detail location LC*)

 

So in this SR, we see RIB Update and FIB Update succeed, but FIB Update on Line Card did not happen. This is unexpected programming problem and we believe this is more like a software issue, not hardware failure.  Replacement is not recommended so far.   As the software version 4.3.4 has been end of software support, so it is hard to involve a development engineer from BU team to take a look.

 

We propose the following guide to help you trouble shoot this kind of issue in case it recurs.

 

Symptom:

*show route x.x.x.x detail , show cef x.x.x.x detail and show cef x.x.x.x detail location LC* commands to check if next-hop is inconsistent.

 

Workaround:

Doing below steps to fix the inconsistency, if previous not work, try next:

 

-- add a static route about x.x.x.x or clear route ipv4 unicast x.x.x.x to trigger a fib upgrade

-- shutdown/no shut the two inconsistent next hop interface  

-- clear cef ipv4 linecard location 0/x/cpu0

-- reload the linecard

 

As for the fpd upgrade failure, it is not clue to identify as hardware failure. Suggest to reload the line card and upgrade again, or configure the fpd auto-upgrade administration configuration command to enable automatic FPD upgrades.  

 

Action Plan :

1) TAC would go on review the collected info and try to reproduce in local lab.

2) Monitor and if issue recurs, follow the workaround above to fix the problem.

 

--

CE found that the sw06.syd02 cannot learn the mac-address from br02.syd02 TenG0/0/2/2. Below is the example. However, not all the customers encountered this problem. Hello Miki,

Thank you for the closure confirmation, it was my pleasure in assisting you with this service request, and I look forward to working with you again in the future.
Below you will find a small summary of the service request:

Problem Description
================
Your A9K-24X10GE-TR= went down on two separate occasions. The cause for each occurrence was different.

Issue 1: On Feb 26, the fiacl process crassed multiple times resulting in a linecard reload.
Issue 2: On Mar 9, shelfmanager deteted a low power situation on the device and as a result, chose to bringdown LC2 to ensure there was enough available power for all other cards.

Resolution Summary
================
Issue 1: PCIe Bus errors are a form of transient hardware error and are classed as a ‘soft error’. This means that they behave and are triaged in a similar manner to a parity error. Performing a physical reseat of the line card will restore services. In this case, no further issues were occurred after the reseat.

Issue 2: We identified that an OIR event had been detected for power supply 0/PM0/0/SP approximately once a month for at least 3 months. The timing of the most recent OIR log aligned with the line card going down. You performed a reseat of the power supply, and the issue has not reoccurred since.

Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any further questions or network issues.

Best Regards,

##################################

Hello Sandeep,

 

Below RTs are used for GRX VRFs.

 
|*import route-target 3491:3491*
*import route-target 3491:1002820*
*import route-target 3491:1002821*
*export route-target 3491:1002821*|

Best regards,

*_Haris Filippakopoulos_*

 

******************************************************************************************

*From:* Sandeep Ajwani [[mailto:sajwani@pccwglobal.com]] 
 **

Dear Haris,

 

We can’t do this as this will cause leaking of VPNv4 routes between the GIA RR’s (dr01.hkg05, dr02.hkg04 for CT and CU) and the MPLS RR’s (dr01.hkg08, dr02.sin02 for MPLS L3 VPNs).

 

Is there a specific GRT that needs to be allowed as we will need to do implement filtering on the VPNv4 DRs (dr01.hkg08 and dr02.sin02) before we can establish a VPNv4 session between br02.hkg15 and the VPNv4 DRs.

 

Regards,

Sandeep Ajwani 

AVP, Engineering

 

*************************************************************************

 

*From:* "Filippakopoulos, Haralabos" <[hfilippakopoulos@pccwglobal.com|mailto:hfilippakopoulos@pccwglobal.com]>



Dear IPE,

 

We have 2 BGP sessions with CU for GRX and Diameter routes. This is normal GRX traffic as we generally configure, nothing custom. The difference is that VRFs are configured on BR routers (BR02.HKG15 & BR04.SIN02).

On Singapore BR router we receive full GRX routing table as it uses dr01.hkg08 and dr02.sin02 but BR02.HKG15 uses only dr01.hkg05 and we don’t get the VPNv4 routing table from any RR. Can we add one of the MPLS VPNv4 RRs for IPVPN customers?

Please let me know if you need further information to review this case?

Apr 09, 2019 20:28;70121:b1b858ce-bb4c-4cd2-acdc-873e46386171;Sandeep, Marco, Pf,

 

Please comment on below suggestion to add BR carrying GIA L3VPN under MPLS L3VPN

 

 

Suggested filtering is on RRs pairs by adding the same specific RT (ie 3491:1) on each GIA vrf on the BR

and adding the same specific RT (ie 3491:2) on each MPLS vrf on the BR

 
|+on MPLS RRs+
 
ip extcommunity-list 1 permit rt 3491:00001
 
route-map VPN04_PE_BR deny 10
match extcommunity 1
route-map VPN04_PE_BR permit 20
 
 
router bgp 65004
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR peer-group
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR remote-as 65004
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR update-source Loopback0
neighbor <br02.sin03> peer-group VPN04_PE_BR
neighbor <br02.hkg15> peer-group VPN04_PE_BR
 
address-family vpnv4
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR send-community both
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR route-reflector-client
neighbor VPN04_PE_BR route-map VPN04_PE_BR in
neighbor <br02.sin03> activate
neighbor <br02.hkg15> activate
 |+on GIA RRs+
 
ip extcommunity-list 2 permit rt 3491:00002
 
route-map VPN04_PE_MPLS deny 10
match extcommunity 1
route-map VPN04_PE_MPLS permit 20
 
 
router bgp 65004
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS peer-group
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS remote-as 65004
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS update-source Loopback0
neighbor <br02.sin03> peer-group VPN04_PE_MPLS
neighbor <br02.hkg15> peer-group VPN04_PE_MPLS
 
address-family vpnv4
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS send-community both
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS route-reflector-client
neighbor VPN04_PE_MPLS route-map VPN04_PE_MPLS in
neighbor <br02.sin03> activate
neighbor <br02.hkg15> activate
 |

Router br04.hkg05 RSP1 (A9K-RSP880-SE)and 0/7/CPU0 (A9K-2x100GE-TR) are down and KaHo brought new spare cards from warehouse to replace them.

We expected that those two cards have problem and we tried to replace them with spare new cards with the same model, however those spare new cards are down also. We also tried to insert new spare line card into free slot 6 already and it is still down. 

Below is the test that we have done during replacement:

1. Replace old RSP1 (A9K-RSP880-SE) with the new spare one (A9K-RSP880-SE) only and found that new RSP1 is still down. RSP1 keeps reboot.

2. Remove new RSP1 from br04.hkg05 first (i.e. RSP1 slot is empty) and remove the old line card from 0/7/CPU0. Insert the new line card (A9K-2x100GE-TR) in line card 6 slot (it is new slot 0/6/cpu0). We found that the new line card is still down and keep in MBI-BOOTING status when the chassis has only one active RSP0.

3. We unseat new line card from line card 6 slot and insert it into line card 7 (0/7/cpu0), the new line card (A9K-2x100GE-TR) is still down and keep in MBI-BOOTING status.

4. We insert new RSP1 into RSP1 slot again and keep the new line card in line card 7 slot (0/7/cpu0). We found that two cards are still down. new line card keeps in MBI-BOOTING status and RSP1 changed to IN-RESET" state after its several reboot.

We have emailed to Cisco Miki to request open TAC case for investigation.

Mar 23, 2019 21:01;635a24491cc605b1fd167d3f;Hi [~accountid:615b48e1bfa2c1006ba9f2f6],

Here are steps for iDRAC setup:

1. Turn on the Dell machine (e.g. Dell r630)

2. Press <F2> during Power-on Self-test (POST)

3. In the System Setup Main Menu page, click iDRAC Settings, the iDRAC Settings page is displayed

4. Click Network, the Network page is displayed

5. Specify the network settings (please see below IP address)
5.1 In Network Settings -> Enable NIC -> select the Enabled option
5.1.1 From the NIC Selection drop-down menu, select the Dedicated
5.2 In IPV4 Settings -> Enable IPv4 -> select the Disable DHCP option
5.2.1 Fill in the static IP Address
5.2.2 Fill in the static Gateway
5.2.3 Fill in the static Subnet Mak

6. Click Back, click Finish, and then click Yes. The network information is saved and the system reboots

Enclosed please find the doc “Setup iDRAC.pdf” for detail steps.

If it is r540, please send us the iDRAC secure password, you can find the password on a sticker on the underside of the system tag with the Service Tag information.

column35:
Hello colleagues,

According to Cisco, IOS-XR triggers the OOM (Out Of Memory) condition the moment the router goes past than less than 10% of available memory on RSP.

Attached you can find the available memory on all of our BRs from a check i've ran couple of weeks ago ([^BRs memory (1).xlsx]).

I am opening this issue because two routers are particularly close to the limit and i thought they might deserve an upgrade:
||Router||RSP||Total memory||Available||
|br03.ash02|A9K-RSP440-TR|6144|951|
|br01.ams02|A9K-RSP440-TR|6144|877|

 

It's also worth to note that the amount of memory is decreasing and there's some alarming downfalls in the historical graphs which make me think memory should decrease without notice.

For instance take a look at what happened on BR01.ASM02 in December and March:

!br01.ams02-module_0_rsp0_cpu0-processor-year.png!

Thank you

Regards

h1. Configuration
{noformat}
!
community-set Lpref-10-Above-Custs-Global
  3491:59001
end-set
!
community-set Lpref-20-Above-Custs-Global 
  3491:59002
end-set
!
route-policy Higher-Lpref-Communities-Global
  if community matches-any Lpref-20-Above-Custs-Global then
    set local-reference 220
  end-if
  if community matches-any Lpref-10-Above-Custs-Global then
    set local-reference 210
  end-if
end-policy
!
route-policy LPref-Communities-Global
  set local-preference 200
  if community matches-any Lpref-10-Below-Custs-Global then
    set local-preference 190
  endif
  if community matches-any Lpref-20-Below-Custs-Global then
    set local-preference 180
  endif
  if community matches-any Lpref-Peers-Global then
    set local-preference 150
  endif
  if community matches-any Lpref-10-Below-Peers-Global then
    set local-preference 70
  endif
  if community matches-any Lpref-20-Below-Peers-Global then
    set local-preference 60
  endif
  if community matches-any GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN then
    set local-preference 0
  endif
end-policy
!
route-policy Scbr-Customer-IN
 # Drop unwanted ASNs
  if (as-path in ASPATH_87) then
    drop
  endif
  # Mark prefixes
  apply Set-Cust-City
  apply Maxas-Limit
  set med 100
  # Blackholing
  if (community matches-any BLACKHOLE) then
    set local-preference 200
    set community (3491:999) additive
    set community (no-export) additive
    set next-hop 192.168.1.253
    done
  endif
  # Drop unwanted prefixes (including long)
  if (destination in PFX-150) then
    drop
  endif
  # Set LPREF
  if (community matches-any LPREF_70) then
    set local-preference 70
  elseif (community matches-any LPREF_80) then
    set local-preference 80
  elseif (community matches-any LPREF_90) then
    set local-preference 90
  elseif (community matches-any 
  else
    set local-preference 200
    # New LPREF communities will eventually replace those above
    apply LPref-Communities-Global
    # Communities to raise LPREF above 200
    apply Higher-Lpref-Communities-Global
  endif
end-policy
!
route-policy BTN_ALIBABA_IN($CUST_PFX)
  if (destination in $CUST_PFX) then
    apply Scbr-Customer-IN
    # Add 1xPREPEND to Telia and NTT
    set community (3491:61111, 3491:60111) additive
  endif
end-policy
!{noformat}
 

Thank you

Regards

*From:* "Michael Ma (huma2)" <huma2@cisco.com>

 
*Date:* Tuesday, March 19, 2019 at 4:49 AM

 
*To:* Sandeep Ajwani <sajwani@pccwglobal.com>

 
*Cc:* "Eric Tam (ertam)" <ertam@cisco.com>

 
*Subject:* Re: CiscoSupportCase_684906686

 

Hello Sandeep,

 

Regarding the case as captioned, I participated in the discussion with TAC and BU engineer during the troubleshooting and they confirmed that C4500/XE 3.6.3E hits this bug. According to the detailed information of this bug, it says that it’s a corner case. Meanwhile, the issue just occurred once so far on PCCWG Cat4500, hence, I personally think the chance to hit the problem should be low.

 

Besides, the codes of C4500 (3.6.3E)/C3850 (3.7.3E) have been recommended for ~3.5 years already, which will reach to the EoL milestone of Last Day of Support (April 30, 2022). So I think it may be time to recommend a new software.

 

In conclusion, it’s recommended to identify a new software code and initiate the corresponding bug-scrub for Catalyst 4500/C3850 fan-out switch respectively. After that, from my understanding, PCCWG may not need to execute the Catalyst fan-out switch software upgrade immediately , but just pre-load the new target image on the flash to address the critical issue in case the problem occurs.

 

Please let me know if there is any question. Thank you.

 

Regards,

Michael

column1: Pentest Remediation Action: 205.252.5.199 - potomac.btnaccess.com
column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
Hi Ian,

 

Following the recently concluded Penetration test,

Host: 205.252.5.199 - potomac.btnaccess.com

was identified to be vulnerable to a couple of attacks and requires immediate remediation. Below is a list of all identified vulnerabilities and recommended remediation actions.

Vulnerabilities

Outdated Apache Software Versions

HTTP Trace Method Enable

 

Outdated Apache Software Versions

An unpatched Apache instance is still susceptible to any attacks discovered and published since the last version was released. When applying security patches to an Apache server, update any other modules installed on the server. A malicious actor can still perform attacks against an Apache web server if its associated modules and other sub-components are out-of-date.

Recommended Action:

Patch the Apache server software and associated modules to the latest known versions.

 

HTTP Trace Method Enable

 

The Hyper Text Transport Protocol (HTTP) TRACE method, by design, causes a web server to echo the contents of an HTTP TRACE request back to the client for debugging purposes. The server responds with the complete request, including HTTP headers, cookies, or authentication data, in the entity-body of a TRACE response.

A malicious actor could use HTTP TRACE functionality and gain access to information in HTTP headers, including cookies and authentication data that may not otherwise be available to scripting as TRACE does not include common protections as cookies do for instance. A malicious actor could combine this with other cross-domain vulnerabilities in web browsers to read sensitive header information from any domains that support the HTTP TRACE method.

 

Recommended Action:

Disable HTTP TRACE support on Internet-facing web servers. Rapid7 recommends limiting input, or whitelisting, the smallest set of HTTP methods required for the application to function properly.

 

Target Date for taking WEB server offline,  2019-03-31

column1: Pentest Remediation Action - Lack of Clickjacking Protections
column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
Hi Jerry,

Following the recently concluded Penetration test, it was discovered that the under-listed web applications lacks clickjacking protection.

This vulnerability would allow a malicious actor hide an interactive layer over an existing application possessing a form or clickable links using an embedded HTML iframe tag. If performed against the login page for a critical system, this attack could give the malicious actor passwords for that system.

*Affected Systems:*

63.221.242.55 - provdb.pccwglobal.com
63.216.149.15 - 63-216-149-15.static.pccwglobal.net
205.252.5.19 - 205-252-5-19.static.pccwglobal.net

Recommended Action:

Recommendations Implement Clickjacking protections by adding the ‘X-Frame-Options’ header to the server configuration. There are three possible values for ‘X-Frame-Options’: • *DEN*Y: The page cannot be displayed in a frame, regardless of the site attempting to do so. If DENY is specified, attempts to load the page in a frame fail when loaded from other sites, as will attempts loaded from the same site.

*SAMEORIGIN:* The page can only be displayed in a frame on the same origin as the page itself. If SAMEORIGIN is specified, the page can still be used in a frame as long as the site including it in a frame is the same as the one serving the page.

 *ALLOW-FROM [URI]:* The page can only be displayed in a frame on the specified origin. Rapid7 also recommends adding defensive code to the web application that ensures the current frame is always the top-most window. 
 

It is also recommended to add defensive code to the web application that ensures the current frame is always the top-most window.

column1: Pentest Remediation Action: TCP Timestamps Enabled
column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
Hi Sandeep,

Following the recently concluded Penetration test, the underlisted hosts were identified to have TCP Timestamps Enabled and requires immediate remediation.

Host: 63.220.13.210

           63.220.13.211

 

TCP Timestamps Enabled

By comparing two TCP packets from the same location with this setting enabled, a malicious actor could approximate the remote host's uptime and determine whether the host has recently been taken down and patched. Some Operating Systems also react to TCP timestamps with recognizable behaviors, which a malicious actor can use to fingerprint the network.

Recommended Action:

Disable TCP timestamp responses. Consult your vendor documentation or follow the directions below. Cisco iOS:

Run the following command to disable TCP timestamps:

no ip tcp timestamp

FreeBSD:

Set the value of ‘net.inet.tcp.rfc1323’ to ‘0’ by running the following command:

sysctl -w net.inet.tcp.rfc1323=0

Additionally, put the following value in the default sysctl configuration file, generally ‘sysctl.conf’: net.inet.tcp.rfc1323=0    

Linux: 

Set the value of ‘net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps’ to ‘0’ by running the following command:

sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps=0

Additionally, put the following value in the default sysctl configuration file, generally ‘sysctl.conf’:

Hi Ian,

Following the recently concluded Penetration test,

Host: 205.177.4.232 - mon-icmp.pccwglobal.com 

was identified to be vulnerable to a couple of attacks and requires immediate remediation. Below is a list of all identified vulnerabilities and recommended remediation actions.

*Vulnerabilities*

Critical Security Patches Missing (Threat Level: Critical)

SMB Message Signing Not Required ((Threat Level: High)

 

Critical Security Patches Missing 

If a user or Administrator does not apply a vulnerability patch to a software or device, it could allow any malicious actor who knows about the vulnerability to exploit it.

Recommended Action:

Update all systems with outstanding patches available. Implement procedures to check and test that all systems are up-to-date with their security patches. However, as the organization grows, a manual system may become unmanageable. Consider implementing a vulnerability management program.

 

SMB Message Signing Not Required 

Server Message Block (SMB) is a widely-used protocol for sharing access to files, printers, ports, and other system resources. SMB message signing allows a system receiving SMB packets to confirm their authenticity. This is done by digitally signing the communications between the hosts. SMB signing can be configured in one of three ways: 

          Disabled entirely (least secure)

           Enabled (but not required)

           Required (most secure) 

SMB signing can prevent Man-in-the-Middle attacks against the SMB protocol. When disabled, a malicious actor can send SMB packets that appear to come from valid users. If this user is an administrative user or in an administrative group, the malicious actor could even gain a connection to the targeted host as the valid user.   

Recommended Action: 

Configure your network to require SMB signing. If this is not possible, SMB signing should be enabled. 

Microsoft Windows - Configure SMB signing 

Configure the Windows system to enable or require SMB signing as appropriate. The steps required for this are system-specific. Consult your vendor instructions or the References section for more information.

Note: Ensure that SMB signing is configured for incoming connections to the server. 

Samba - Configure SMB signing 

Configure Samba to enable or require SMB signing, as appropriate. To enable or require SMB signing, open the Samba configuration file, typically ‘smb.conf’, in the global section, and add the code: 
 * Enabled: server signing = auto
 * Required: server signing = mandatory 

For other network configurations, consult the vendor documentation.

column35:
Hi Jerry,

Following the recently concluded Penetration test,

63.223.143.3 - saa01.pccwglobal.com

was identified to be vulnerable to a couple of attacks and needs to be remediated as soon as possible. Below is a list of all identified vulnerabilities and recommended remediation actions.

Vulnerabilities

Hosts with Expired Certificates

Hosts Using Weak Ciphers and Deprecated Protocols

Outdated Apache Software Versions

HTTP Trace Method Enable

 

Host With Expired certificates

During a Man-in-the-Middle attack, a malicious actor could leverage a service that accepts weak protocols and cipher suites to downgrade a user's connection to a weaker protocol or cipher suite, even if stronger connections are also supported. This downgrade could increase the malicious actor's chances of decrypting the secure web communication.

 

To keep with best practices and prevent opportunities for malicious spoofing, all hosted TLS/SSL certificates should be kept up-to-date with a valid start and expiration date.

 

Recommended Action:

It is recommended to obtain a new certificate and have it installed on the affected server(s). The exact instructions for obtaining a new certificate will depend on organizational requirements. An organization may have its own internal Certificate Authority. If not, a certificate may be purchased from a trusted external Certificate Authority. After a new certificate file has been issued, it must be installed on the affected server(s).

 

*Hosts Using Weak Ciphers and Deprecated Protocols:*

When sensitive data, such as credit card numbers or Personally Identifiable Information (PII), is transmitted over an encrypted SSL or TLS connection, using a weak protocol or cipher puts that information at risk of decryption.

 

A malicious actor could leverage a service that accepts weak protocols and cipher suites to downgrade a user's connection to a weaker protocol or cipher suite

 

Recommended Action:

Disable support for connections using weak protocols and ciphers, including:
 * SSL Version 2 or 3
 * TLS Version 1.0
 * ADH, AECDH, or RC4 ciphers
 * Any cipher suite using less than 128 bits of keyspace

Ideally, SSL and TLS services should only support connections using the following protocols and cipher suites:
 * TLS Version 1.2 or higher
 * Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption, using at least 128 bits of keyspace
 * RSA with AES encryption, using at least 128 bits of keyspace

Note: If weak protocols or cipher suites are supported alongside strong protocols and cipher suites, those weaker connections could be leveraged in downgrade attacks.

Outdated Apache Software Versions

An unpatched Apache instance is still susceptible to any attacks discovered and published since the last version was released. When applying security patches to an Apache server, update any other modules installed on the server. A malicious actor can still perform attacks against an Apache web server if its associated modules and other sub-components are out-of-date.

Recommended Action:

Patch the Apache server software and associated modules to the latest known versions.

HTTP Trace Method Enable

 

The Hyper Text Transport Protocol (HTTP) TRACE method, by design, causes a web server to echo the contents of an HTTP TRACE request back to the client for debugging purposes. The server responds with the complete request, including HTTP headers, cookies, or authentication data, in the entity-body of a TRACE response. 

A malicious actor could use HTTP TRACE functionality and gain access to information in HTTP headers, including cookies and authentication data that may not otherwise be available to scripting as TRACE does not include common protections as cookies do for instance. A malicious actor could combine this with other cross-domain vulnerabilities in web browsers to read sensitive header information from any domains that support the HTTP TRACE method.

 

Recommended Action:

Disable HTTP TRACE support on Internet-facing web servers. Rapid7 recommends limiting input, or whitelisting, the smallest set of HTTP methods required for the application to function properly.

column35:
Hi Hon,

 

Following the recently concluded Penetration test, the underlisted host was identified to to be using an insecure service(FTP) and requires immediate remediation.

Host: 63.218.228.229(Threat Level: Moderate)

 

Insecure Services in Use

 

Insecure services, such as Hyper Text Transfer Protocol (HTTP), File Transfer Protocol (FTP), and Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) transmit user credentials and other sensitive information in cleartext.

A malicious actor intercepting or ‘sniffing’ network traffic can capture this unencrypted data transmitted with these services. Validation

 

Recommended Action:

 

Implement a plan to remove all insecure services and replace them with secure alternatives. Use HTTPS instead of HTTP whenever passing sensitive information. Replace FTP with SFTP, and Telnet with SSH. If using SNMP, ensure SNMPv3 is used to enable encryption. Use authentication with SNMPv3 to ensure data is not modified in transit.

 

If it is not possible to replace an insecure service, isolate systems required to use the service.

column11: This project is designed to track and manage all work specific to production AS3491 network devices. This include incident management, problem management, change management (CMR and Emergency CMR) and service requests (SR) involving these devices.
column35:
Summary * 
A vulnerability in the IPv6 processing code of Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload.
 
 The vulnerability is due to incorrect handling of specific IPv6 hop-by-hop options. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a malicious IPv6 packet to or through the affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the device to reload, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device.

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability.

This advisory is available at the following link:
 [https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-20180926-ipv6hbh]
This advisory is part of the September 26, 2018, release of the Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software Security Advisory Bundled Publication, which includes 12 Cisco Security Advisories that describe 13 vulnerabilities. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see [Cisco Event Response: September 2018 Semiannual Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software Security Advisory Bundled Publication|http://tools.cisco.com/security/center/viewErp.x?alertId=ERP-69981].

Affected Products * 
h2. Vulnerable Products
This vulnerability affects devices that are running a vulnerable version of Cisco IOS or IOS XE Software and are configured with an IPv6 address.
 
 For more information about which Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software releases are vulnerable, see the [Fixed Software|https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-20180926-ipv6hbh#fixed] section of this advisory.

interface GigabitEthernet4

ipv6 enable
ipv6 traffic-filter HBH_ACL in
!
ipv6 access-list HBH_ACL
deny ipv6 any any hbh
permit ipv6 any any
!

Example Using CoPP:
!
class-map match-all HBH_ACL
match access-group name HBH_ACL
!
policy-map DROP-UNAUTHORIZED-INFRA-TRAFFIC  class HBH_ACL
  police cir 32000 bc 1500 be 1500 conform-action drop  exceed-action drop  violate-action drop !

permit ipv6 any any hbh
!
control-plane
service-policy input DROP-UNAUTHORIZED-INFRA-TRAFFIC 
!"

Below are the steps for renaming a CR router to a BR / VAR router.
 # Please rename the CR router to BR/VAR router in the respective Installation book. Contact Brian Tam to assist.
 # Please send email to DNS Admin to change the DNS forwards and DNS reverses from the CR router to the respective BR/VAR router.
 # Please send email to Engineering to rename all references of the CR router to BR/VAR router in ProvDB and relevant DB’s (Rancid, Prefix-list DB, etc).
 # Please send email to Steve and Wahyudi to change the ACS requests from CR router to BR/VAR router.
 # Please update Hostname in the router from CR to BR/VAR router.
 # Please update Interface Descriptions on either end to reflect router change from CR to BR/VAR.
 # Please open ticket with the underlying co-location provider to re-label the CR router to BR/VAR router for future reference.
 # Rename the routers on the MRV via the oobtelnet script on teton.
 # Rename the customer names in ProvDB from the old CR to the new BR/VAR.
 # Shutdown any links between BR-VAR routers after the renaming has taken place.
 # Check on the RR configuration as CR’s are IPv4 RR’s and after renaming to BR/VAR they become RR-clients.
